(3) Recency rule: A&P and Pathophysiology must be earned within 5 years of applying (applicant's 2026 A&P is fine; 2001-2005 coursework irrelevant since micro/stats/nutrition/psych have no stated recency limit). (4) Exact start date: Spring 2027 term start published as January 11, 2027 on RCoN pre-nursing page (Spring 2026 analog began Jan 12); prior 2027-01-15 was approximate. programs.notes: (1) DEADLINE: Confirmed Nov 15, 2026 for the Spring/Jan 2027 cohort (not Nov 1) - verbatim from official page: 'Application Deadlines - Fall: July 1, Spring: November 15.' Page also says applications are 'accepted on a rolling basis, so you can apply at any time,' i.e. rolling review up to that firm final deadline. (2) APP FEE: No fee is mentioned anywhere in Loyola's exhaustive official ABSN application-requirements list (transcripts, GPA, personal statement, prereq form, 2 references, resume/CV) - strong evidence it's $0. Corroborated indirectly: Loyola's other nursing grad programs (DNP/MSN/PhD), processed by the same Graduate and Professional Enrollment Management office as ABSN, are confirmed $0. Not found as an explicit 'ABSN application fee: $0' sentence, so treat as very likely but not ironclad. (3) 5-YEAR RECENCY: Confirmed explicit rule, but NARROWER than a blanket 'all science prereqs' rule - the 'Completed within 5 years of entering the program' tag applies ONLY to 4 specific rows (verified via raw HTML table structure, not just prose): Organic Chemistry/Chemistry for Health Professionals, A&P I & II, Microbiology, and Developmental Psychology/Lifespan Development. It does NOT apply to History, Statistics, Philosophy, College Writing, or Theology - those can be from any point in the applicant's academic history, including 2001-2005 UW-Madison coursework. Applicant's 2026 A&P I/II, Micro (completing Aug 1 2026), and Lifespan Psych are all comfortably within the 5-year window for a Jan 2027 start. HOWEVER see chem flag in notes - a separate, non-recency risk. (4) ONLINE A&P LAB: Could NOT be definitively resolved despite thorough search of the official prerequisites page (fetched twice, plus raw HTML/table inspection), the PDF prerequisite form, program blog content, and forum discussions. The ONLY concrete exclusion language found: (a) 'Courses that are taken via a self-directed, online learning platform will not be accepted' (stated twice on the official page) and (b) science courses described as 'fundamental, essential, or survey' are generally rejected. Neither statement explicitly addresses a structured, instructor-led online lab from a regionally accredited institution (as opposed to a self-paced platform like Sophia/StraighterLine) - which is what the applicant's A&P I/II labs sound like. Separately, 'all students complete simulation labs and clinicals in person' - but that refers to the ABSN PROGRAM's own nursing simulation/clinical labs during the 16 months, not prerequisite science courses, and applies equally to onsite and hybrid tracks. Set to 'unknown.' ACTION ITEM: the official prereq page names a specific contact for exactly this kind of question - Jorgia Connor, PhD, RN - email via the nursing admissions office before applying to get this in writing. (5) DOWNERS GROVE / HYBRID TRACK: Historically real and distinct - Loyola launched an online-didactic 'Hybrid' ABSN track based at a dedicated Downers Grove, IL site in 2017-2018 (with partner Orbis Education): non-clinical coursework online, but students travel to the site a few times/week for in-person skills/simulation labs and proctored exams; clinicals at area facilities. This Hybrid track is CONFIRMED STILL ACTIVE for 2026-2027 cohorts per Loyola's current official Bursar fee schedule, which lists a distinct (lower) 'Hybrid Program' fee schedule alongside 'Onsite' fees for both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 starts. However, the current official ABSN program overview page (freshly fetched, 2026 copyright) only describes the choice generically as 'hybrid option with classes online or a fully on-campus experience,' gives a single Maywood address, and does not name 'Downers Grove' explicitly - so cannot 100% confirm the hybrid track's physical lab site is still literally Downers Grove today versus possibly consolidated onto the Maywood Health Sciences Campus. Same deadlines (Jul 1 / Nov 15) and same prerequisites appear to govern both tracks; no separate hybrid-specific deadline found. Recommend confirming current hybrid-track lab location directly with admissions if this format matters. | MAJOR DISCREPANCIES VS KNOWN DATA: (a) prereq_extras was empty in our database and that was a real gap - Loyola requires 5 non-science categories beyond the 'standard' tags: History/literary knowledge, Philosophical knowledge, College writing, and (notably) Theological/religious knowledge, none previously captured. (b) Nutrition is NOT a Loyola ABSN prerequisite per the current official page - it only appears as an in-program course ('Clinical Nutrition for Nursing Practice,' 2cr, semester 1 of the ABSN curriculum), so our 'nutrition required' flag looks wrong; harmless for this applicant since she already has it, but the database should be corrected. (c) A general 'Intro to Psychology' requirement appeared on an older-looking PDF prerequisite form (filename suggests 2017) but NOT on the current (2026) official webpage, which only lists 'Developmental Psychology or Lifespan Development' - treating the current webpage as authoritative and dropping the standalone psych requirement, but flagging the conflict since the PDF is still linked from Loyola's own site. APPLICANT-SPECIFIC RISK FLAG (material): Loyola's chemistry prerequisite is specifically 'Organic Chemistry OR Chemistry for Health Professionals' - NOT general/intro chemistry. The applicant's 2026 course was 'General Chemistry.' Depending on that course's actual depth/content, it may or may not satisfy this requirement, especially given Loyola's explicit warning that 'fundamental, essential, or survey' science courses are 'generally not going to be accepted.' This is a real, undetermined risk parallel to the online-lab question - confirm with Jorgia Connor/admissions before relying on this course. CNA SCREENING (2026-07-15): NOT required - no CNA/nurse-aide requirement appears on the official ABSN application page, prerequisite tables, or catalog curriculum; only BLS certification (for clinicals) appears. RELIGIOUS/THEOLOGY NUANCE: Loyola Chicago is Catholic/Jesuit. Verified specifically for the ABSN track: the in-program 67-credit ABSN nursing curriculum itself does NOT include any theology/religious-studies coursework, and ABSN students are explicitly exempted from the general Loyola core curriculum and UNIV 101 (catalog.luc.edu). BUT a 3-credit 'Theological or religious knowledge' course IS required as a pre-admission PREREQUISITE (no recency limit, grade C- minimum) - so required_coursework=true is correct, but only at the admission-gate level, not within the nursing program itself. Because the applicant's known coursework is from UW-Madison (secular public) plus 2026 science/quant courses, she may well NOT have a qualifying theology/religious-studies course on file, and likely also lacks a dedicated Philosophy course - confirm against her actual transcript or add each (e.g., affordable community-college or online 3-credit courses; neither carries the 5-year recency restriction, so old coursework counts if it exists). TUITION BASIS: $72,120 total = $18,030/term x 4 terms; confirmed identical for BOTH Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 (Jan 2027) cohort entries, and identical for Onsite vs Hybrid tracks (only fees differ by track, not tuition). FEES: fees_total ~$2,140-2,200 for the Onsite track (Student Development $206 + Fitness Center $194 + Technology $135 per semester x 4, plus $60 graduation fee); Hybrid track fees are lower (~$848, no Fitness Center fee, smaller Student Development fee). NOT included: mandatory Student Health Insurance ($3,869/yr), typically waivable with proof of existing coverage - a possible real cost if applicant doesn't maintain independent insurance. START DATE: Could not find an ABSN-specific exact start day on any official ABSN page (only 'begins in January'); 2027-01-19 is from Loyola's official university-wide Spring 2027 academic calendar ('Spring semester begins Tuesday, January 19, 2027'), which conflicts with the prior value of 2027-01-15 - accelerated cohorts sometimes start on/near but not exactly with the general semester; confirm directly before treating either date as final. RANKING: US News #13 / NCLEX 93.7% (2023, first-time) both independently confirmed via official luc.edu pages. DEPOSIT: could not locate any ABSN-specific enrollment deposit amount or timing on official pages despite dedicated searching - a deposit is very likely required post-acceptance as is standard, but left null rather than guessed; confirm with admissions.

programs.notes: (1) DEADLINE/START: Confirmed precisely. Spring/Jan cohort 'Regular Decision' deadline = August 15 (2026), per official nursing.pitt.edu/admissions/deadlines/ (also a 'Priority' deadline of April 15 existed, already passed). Start date confirmed as Monday, Jan 11, 2027, per Pitt University Registrar's official 2026-2027 Academic Calendar (spring term first day of classes). Both figures match prior database values exactly. (2) PA CLEARANCES TIMELINE: Four clearances required before clinical: Act 33 (PA Child Abuse History, via PA Child Welfare Info Solution), Act 34 (PA Criminal Record Check, via PATCH), Act 73 (FBI fingerprint criminal history, via IdentoGo, DHS service code 1KG756), and Act 168 (PA sexual misconduct/abuse disclosure, required specifically for Community Health clinical placement). For ABSN specifically, Pitt's official clearances page states students must 'submit all clearances by the deadline communicated by academic advisor, prior to program start' (no fixed public date - advisor sets it individually, unlike traditional 4-year BSN which has sophomore/senior-year benchmarks that don't apply to the 1-year ABSN calendar). Critical timing risk: Act 73 FBI results can take up to 12 weeks to return, so if accepted (decisions likely trickle in after Aug 15), applicant should initiate all four clearances immediately upon acceptance to be safe before Jan 11. Clearances are valid 5 years but some clinical sites require annual renewal; student bears all costs. (3) NURSINGCAS DETAILS: Pitt ABSN uses NursingCAS exclusively. Required materials confirmed via official admissions/application-process page: completed application, official transcripts from every institution attended, 2 letters of professional recommendation, resume, and one personal essay (goals-focused, no stated word/page limit). No TEAS or HESI exam requirement appears anywhere on Pitt's own current application-requirements or FAQ pages (contradicts older third-party aggregator claims of a 'TEAS 70%' cutoff - likely stale info from a prior cycle; recommend applicant verify directly since this affects test-prep time budget). GPA minimum ~3.0 in the prior bachelor's degree (found via search-indexed official content; the specific admissions-info subpage 404'd on direct fetch so this is slightly less certain than other figures). Fee: Pitt-specific supplemental fee is $50 (confirmed); NursingCAS undergraduate base fee for the 2026-27 cycle is $70 for first program (per NursingCAS/Liaison fee schedule), giving ~$120 total - close to but not identical to the $125 previously on file (likely a prior-cycle base-fee figure). $250 non-refundable deposit due upon acceptance (confirmed). No interview requirement found for ABSN (Pitt's page explicitly states interviews ARE required for MSN/DNP/PhD but is silent on interview for ABSN, a meaningful contrast). (4) ONLINE A&P LAB ACCEPTANCE: NOT FOUND despite exhaustive search of nursing.pitt.edu's program page, FAQ page (fetched directly, verbatim), curriculum/catalog pages, and clearances pages. Every official source that lists the Chemistry/A&P/Microbiology prerequisites simply says each 'includes a lab' with zero language distinguishing online/virtual vs. in-person delivery. The recurring official phrase is that 'academic advisors will work closely with you to establish the most suitable course plan,' strongly suggesting Pitt evaluates lab format case-by-case per transcript rather than publishing a blanket rule. One indirect, non-conclusive data point: Pitt's clinical BLS/CPR policy explicitly REJECTS online-only certification ('due to the possible need to perform CPR on an actual patient, an on-line course will not be accepted') - a different requirement (clinical-readiness cert, not academic prereq coursework) but suggestive of a generally cautious institutional posture toward remote hands-on training. Given this is a genuine hard-blocker risk and the deadline is only ~1 month out, this MUST be resolved by directly emailing ABSN@pitt.edu or calling 412-624-4586 / 1-888-747-0794 and getting a written answer before relying on this program. | TUITION BASIS: $79,431 total confirmed as out-of-state basis (3 terms x $26,477/term), directly verified on tuition.pitt.edu's official School of Nursing tuition page (2025-26 published rate; 2026-27 rate not yet posted but typically a small inflationary bump - treat as a floor, not ceiling). WI residency does NOT reduce this - Pitt has no WI tuition reciprocity, consistent with this database's existing rule that only UW-Milwaukee (WI) and UT Health Houston (TX) get in-state treatment. Fees confirmed exactly: $2,655 = $885/term x 3 (Transportation $155 + Student Activity $100 + Wellness/Rec $405 + Computing/Network $225, all per term). Conway Nursing Scholarship (~$8,000-8,333/yr, guaranteed upon admission per Pitt's official program page, quoted twice identically) is NOT netted into tuition_total - apply separately if modeling net cost. BSN ranked #8 nationally (tie) by US News, confirmed via nursing.pitt.edu/about/rankings/. Religious affiliation confirmed NONE - Pitt is one of PA's four 'state-related' public universities (with Penn State, Temple, Lincoln); no religion/theology coursework appears anywhere in the prerequisite list. CNA SCREENING (2026-07-15): NOT required - no CNA/nurse-aide certification or course requirement appears in the NursingCAS application materials, FAQ, curriculum, or clearance requirements; the only certification is BLS (which must be an in-person course, not online-only) for clinicals. IMPORTANT CORRECTION vs prior database: stats and psych were marked FALSE in the existing record - this appears WRONG. Pitt's official prerequisite list (confirmed identically across 4 independent official-content fetches) explicitly requires 'Statistics (descriptive, probability, & inferential)' (3 cr) and 'Psychology' (3 cr) as standalone standard prerequisites. Recommend updating both to TRUE. Good news for the applicant: her 2026 Statistics course directly satisfies Pitt's stats requirement. Her 'Lifespan Developmental Psychology' course very likely satisfies Pitt's generic 'Psychology' requirement too (Pitt does not ask for a specifically-titled lifespan/development course, just 'Psychology'), but since Pitt evaluates equivalency via academic advisor review rather than a public course-title whitelist, confirm directly. Lifespan and nutrition are correctly FALSE either way - Pitt requires neither as a distinct prerequisite. prereq_extras (Human Genetics, Pathophysiology, English Composition-technical) match the prior record and are confirmed accurate; added 'General elective credits (6 cr)' as a minor extra not previously captured (any-subject filler, unlikely a real constraint). NOTE: Human Genetics (w/ lab) and Pathophysiology are NOT in the applicant's completed 2026 coursework - these are real outstanding prereqs for her at Pitt, and with an Aug 15, 2026 deadline plus prereqs generally needing completion before program start (Jan 11, 2027), she would need to line up both this fall - tight but conceivably feasible; the technical-writing English Comp requirement also needs transcript-level verification against her UW-Madison coursework. NCLEX figure (92.51%, AY2024-25) comes from Google's index of nursing.pitt.edu's certification-pass-rate page; the live page 404'd on direct fetch (site underwent URL restructure - many /programs/absn/* paths dead; current structure is /academics/accelerated-2nd-degree-bsn-absn/ and /absn-faqs/), but two independent search queries returned identical figures (92.51% 2024-25, 97.17% 2023-24, 93.16% 2022-23, 87.34% 2021-22) - reasonably strong corroboration despite not being a first-party page read. Rate is for the School of Nursing undergraduate cohort collectively (Pittsburgh+Greensburg+Johnstown, likely traditional+ABSN combined), not ABSN-specific. prereq_recency_years=10: science prerequisites within 10 years per official content. URGENCY: deadline ~1 month away (Aug 15). Top priorities: (a) resolve the online-lab question directly with ABSN@pitt.edu NOW - potential hard blocker on an otherwise well-suited program; (b) verify whether Human Genetics + Pathophysiology can still be completed before Jan 11, 2027 and whether in-progress-at-application is acceptable for them (in_progress_ok=true reflects that Pitt allows prereqs in progress at application generally, per advisor-mediated course planning language, but the two missing courses make this material); (c) if proceeding, submit NursingCAS with buffer before Aug 15 and be ready to move fast on PA clearances (Act 73 alone can take 12 weeks) immediately upon acceptance.

programs.notes: PRACTICAL DEADLINE FOR JAN 2027: Tulane does not publish per-cohort deadlines far in advance. As of this research (mid-July 2026), only the Fall 2026 cohort's dates are live (general application deadline July 17, 2026; classes begin Aug 31, 2026); the Spring 2027 nursing-specific calendar/deadline page returns 404 and is not yet listed on SoPA's academic-calendars index. However, Tulane's registrar DOES confirm the Spring 2027 semester's first day of classes as January 11, 2027, explicitly flagged for the Program of Nursing (term concludes April 28, 2027) - this corrects the prior 2027-01-15 figure. Applying the Fall-2026 cycle's observed offsets (general deadline = 45 days pre-start; LCMC deadline = 67 days pre-start; LCMC deposit = 14 days after LCMC deadline; general deposit = 31 days pre-start) to Jan 11, 2027 yields ESTIMATES (not officially confirmed): general application deadline ~Nov 27, 2026; LCMC Nurse Scholars deadline ~Nov 5, 2026; LCMC deposit ~Nov 19, 2026; general enrollment deposit ~Dec 11, 2026. Applicant should call admissions (nursingadm@tulane.edu / 504-988-5558) around Sept-Oct 2026 once real Spring 2027 dates post, and should not let the application slip past ~November 2026. LCMC NURSE SCHOLARS CYCLE: Real, active, integrated into the same nursing application (no separate application, but its own earlier deadline - observed ~3 weeks ahead of the general deadline). It funds up to 150 total BSN Nurse Scholars cumulatively (not confirmed how many of the 150 remain as of mid-2026). It is NOT a grant - it's a forgivable loan: LCMC pays tuition + required fees directly (capped at $17,500/semester, $70,000 program lifetime), forgiven in full only if the graduate completes a 2-year full-time RN work commitment at an LCMC-matched New Orleans hospital (assigned via a Match Day ~2-3 months before graduation); unfulfilled commitments must be repaid with interest. It should in principle be available for a Jan 2027 start (the program is described as ongoing/cohort-agnostic, not restricted to specific terms), but eligibility is explicitly conditioned on 'LCMC Health funding must be available' - applicant should confirm current funding status directly with admissions when applying. ONLINE A&P LAB POLICY: CONFIRMED ACCEPTED. Direct quote from Tulane's official SoPA Track FAQ: 'Are prerequisite nursing courses taken online accepted? Prerequisite nursing courses taken online from an accredited college or university may be transferred for credit, regardless of whether they were completed online or in person.' This is an unambiguous official statement that the applicant's online A&P I/II labs are accepted on equal footing with in-person labs, provided the institution is accredited and the course meets the C-grade/10-year-recency standards. NOT a hard blocker. (Separately, Tulane's own nursing-program lab/clinical courses taken AFTER admission do require in-person attendance - but that's about their own curriculum, not the prerequisite-transfer policy, and doesn't affect this applicant's eligibility.) | KNOWN-DATA CORRECTIONS: (1) start_date corrected 2027-01-15 -> 2027-01-11 (Tulane registrar explicitly ties Jan 11, 2027 to the Program of Nursing; Jan 15 is a Friday, an atypical cohort-start day, while Jan 11 is a Monday). (2) rolling corrected true -> false: this is NOT continuous rolling admission; it's three fixed annual start dates (Jan/May/Sept), each with a real deadline that Tulane simply hasn't published yet for a term 6 months out (only ~2 months' lead time is typical). (3) tuition_total updated $64,980 -> $65,280, reflecting the official newly-issued 2026-2027 rate ($1,088/credit x 60 credits, PDF dated 2026-03-19, explicitly covers Fall 2026-Summer 2027, i.e., the exact window spanning a Jan 2027 start) vs the older $1,083/credit rate the prior pass used. (4) fees_total refined to $4,720 = $3,836 mandatory per-semester fees (Academic Support Services $560 + Student Activity $107 [12+ credit-hour bracket, which a 60cr/4-semester full-time accelerated load always hits] + Campus Health $292, x4 semesters) + $884 one-time program fees (lab supply/uniform/operational/clinical-compliance/licensure/graduation). Excludes books (~$300/semester, variable) and health insurance (required unless adequate alternative coverage is shown; premium not published). (5) prereq_extras populated (was empty) - net effect on THIS applicant is minor since she already holds a completed bachelor's degree. CNA SCREENING (2026-07-15): NOT required - Tulane explicitly states no prior healthcare experience is needed to be eligible for the ABSN, and no certifications (CNA or otherwise, including BLS) appear in the admission requirements; certifications array is accordingly empty at the admission stage (clinical-compliance items are handled post-admission via the one-time program fees). ACCREDITATION FLAG (new finding, not in prior pass): Tulane's own FAQ states the Program of Nursing is 'in the process of becoming' CCNE-accredited, i.e. NOT YET formally accredited as of this research - worth re-checking close to application time since accreditation can affect financial aid and downstream BSN-to-NP program acceptance. This is also why nclex_first_time is null: the program launched Fall 2024 and no first-time pass-rate data is published yet (first graduates too recent). A third-party aggregator (absnprograms.org) and some AI search summaries state prereqs must be within 'seven years,' conflicting with Tulane's own pages (checked independently across 3 separate official URLs, all say 'ten years') - trusted the official, directly-fetched source. Applicant's relevant track is SoPA (School of Professional Advancement), not NTC (Newcomb-Tulane College, current Tulane undergrads only) - all figures above are SoPA-track. Tulane's nursing site recently reorganized its URLs (old paths like /prerequisites, /admission-requirements, /affordability now 301-redirect to /program-overview or new /sopa-track-* pages); this report cites current live URLs. app_fee ($40) and deposit ($25) are drawn from SoPA's general (not nursing-specific) fee schedule - nursing wasn't broken out separately, so treat with slightly lower confidence than the nursing-specific tuition/fee figures. Program requires relocation to New Orleans; in-person attendance 2-3 days/week; ~45 hrs/week time commitment; working while enrolled explicitly discouraged; does not accept international students; does not accept transfer credit for professional nursing courses (only prerequisites); no part-time option. Religious: confirmed private, nonsectarian (administered under an 1884 act separating it from religious control; no religious affiliation today), no theology/religion coursework anywhere in prereqs or curriculum.

General Chemistry explicitly satisfies it, and NO chemistry lab is required (the prereq list attaches '+ Lab' only to A&P I, A&P II, and Microbiology; chemistry is a 3-cr lecture course). The applicant's 2026 General Chemistry with in-person lab (grade A) fully satisfies this requirement. The database's prereq_extra 'Organic Chemistry with lab' is WRONG and should be removed. 2) DEADLINE/START CONFIRMED: Official page (fetched live July 2026, identical in Feb 2026 Wayback snapshot) states 'Application Deadline: November 1'; applications accepted year-round. Program runs 4 successive semesters incl. summer = January (spring) cohort start. Nov 1, 2026 deadline for Jan 2027 confirmed. Exact first day of Spring 2027 classes is NOT yet published (registrar calendar shows TBD; Spring 2026 full-semester classes began Jan 12, so 2027-01-15 is approximate, likely ~Jan 11-19). Note: the page has shown only ONE deadline (Nov 1) continuously since early 2026 — the prior note claiming 'Jan and Aug starts' is unsupported by current official materials; treat as single annual January cohort. 3) ONLINE A&P LAB POLICY — UNKNOWN: after exhaustive search of the program page, 2026-27 bulletin, SON admissions pages, and the ABSN onboarding deck, Loyola publishes NO policy on whether prerequisite science labs may be online vs in-person. Transfer rule states only: C or better and less than 10 years old, with an 'individual gap analysis' per applicant. Given Loyola's own didactic delivery is online and no modality restriction is stated anywhere, acceptance is plausible (consistent with DB's online_lab_conf=0.9 belief) but UNVERIFIED — applicant should email advisor Nick Jackson (nbjackso@loyno.edu, 504-865-3202) to confirm her online A&P I/II labs. 4) THEOLOGY — NOT REQUIRED: ABSN is 54 credits of nursing-major courses only; 'a bachelor's (or higher) degree in a field other than nursing fulfills the requirements for most Loyola core courses.' No theology/religious-studies course appears in the ABSN curriculum or prerequisites (NURS G432 'Health in Mind, Body & Spirit', 2 cr, is a nursing course). The Religious Studies core option applies only to the traditional 4-yr BSN. 5) CNA — NOT REQUIRED: no CNA certification or CNA training appears anywhere in Loyola's ABSN admission requirements, prerequisite list, bulletin, or admitted-student compliance packet (which requires only: LSBN student license application + background check, SON background check, physical exam, urine drug screen, BLS from AHA/Red Cross, health insurance, immunizations). The next cohort after today starts ~Aug 25, 2027, about 19 months later than the applicant's Jan 2027 target, so this program cannot meet the stated goal at all and is included for comparison purposes only, per instructions. | PROGRAM NAME/STRUCTURE: Official Hunter branding is 'Accelerated Second-Degree Nursing Program (A2D)' -- A2D = Accelerated Second Degree, NOT 'Accelerated to Doctorate'. It is a distinct 51-credit, 18-month track for applicants who already hold a non-nursing bachelor's degree, clearly separate from the 4-year 'Generic' BS track and the RN-to-BS completion track. EXAM: Hunter uses the NLN Pre-Admission Nursing Examination (PAX/NEX), NOT TEAS/HESI/Kaplan, so the schema's 'exam' enum was forced to null -- actual requirement recorded here and in prereq_extras. Admission is ranked by composite score: 50% cumulative GPA + 50% NLN NEX score; exam must be completed by Feb 28 of the application cycle, with scores received by Hunter by Mar 1. DUAL APPLICATION SYSTEM: A2D applicants (not already enrolled CUNY/Hunter students) must submit BOTH a NursingCAS application ($50 first-processed-app fee) AND a separate CUNY transfer/undergraduate application via the CUNY Application portal (~$70 fee) -- both due Feb 1; app_fee reflects the combined $120. REFERENCES/INTERVIEW: no letters-of-recommendation or interview requirement found anywhere in official sources -- NursingCAS confirms a 'References' tab only appears if a program requires it, and Hunter's own admission-procedure documents never mention references; admission appears to rest purely on GPA + NLN NEX composite + the career goal statement (no explicit word count found for A2D specifically; a ~500-word guideline exists only for Hunter's GRADUATE nursing personal statements). FEES: fees_total left null -- could not confirm a program-specific total; general CUNY mandatory fees (technology/activity/consolidated services) run roughly $226/semester for full-time undergrads, and the 18-month A2D spans multiple terms (Fall/Winter/Spring/Summer/Fall), so total mandatory fees are likely several hundred dollars but not independently confirmed per-term. IN-PROGRESS: max 2 prerequisite courses may be in-progress at application time; all prereqs complete by June 1 before Fall entry and not during the immediately-preceding summer. NCLEX: figures are inconsistent across sources -- Wikipedia (citing NY State Office of the Professions) reports 87.6% first-time pass for 2025 grads (127/145, used above); a Hunter press release separately touted 'more than 98%' for 2024 grads and a ~88% ten-year average -- flagged for caution, methodologies/cohorts may differ. TUITION: 51 credits x $620/credit (CUNY non-resident/out-of-state per-credit rate, confirmed on Hunter's official Tuition & Fees page) = $31,620, matching prior known data exactly. WI residency does not qualify for CUNY's in-state $305/credit rate (NY residency required), so non-resident rate correctly applied. GPA: 3.2 minimum. CLINICAL CLEARANCE (post-acceptance, not part of the initial application packet): BLS (American Heart Association ONLY -- Red Cross not accepted), background check via CastleBranch, and immunizations/TB screening/health insurance/HIPAA training are all required before starting clinical coursework -- reflected in certifications/background_check but note these apply pre-clinical, not at application. hunter.cuny.edu and allnurses.com both returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches throughout this research (bot protection); content was retrieved via Google search snippets and an r.jina.ai reader proxy against the same official URLs, so citations point to the original hunter.cuny.edu/CUNY URLs actually consulted.

Every source repeats the same general line — 'online courses can be accepted if taken at a regionally accredited college or university' — with no explicit carve-out addressing whether the LAB component itself may be online/virtual (Labster, at-home kit) vs. must be in-person. No source anywhere states an in-person-lab requirement either. Circumstantial signal leans toward acceptance: Drexel's own in-house A&P II course for health-science majors (HSCI 207) itself uses an online lab format, and no competing 'in-person lab required' language exists anywhere in Drexel's public materials (which would be unusual phrasing to omit if it were a hard rule, given how common the question is). Given both of the applicant's A&P labs were online, this must be confirmed in writing (askcnhp@drexel.edu or enroll@drexel.edu) before treating Drexel as safe — do not rely on the favorable circumstantial read alone. (2) RECENCY: Drexel uses a SPLIT window, not a single number: Anatomy, Physiology, and Microbiology must be completed within 5 years of the program start; ALL other prerequisites (Chemistry, Nutrition, Statistics, Developmental/Lifespan Psychology, English Composition) must be within 10 years. All of the applicant's 2026-completed coursework (Chem, A&P I, A&P II, Stats, Nutrition, Lifespan Psych) and in-progress Microbiology are trivially within both windows. The one latent risk: if the applicant's required English Composition credit is among the old 2001-2005 UW-Madison coursework rather than a 2026 course, it would be 20+ years old and exceed Drexel's 10-year window for 'other' prerequisites — applicant should confirm the exact term of their English Comp credit and be prepared to retake it if it predates ~2017. (3) RELIGIOUS: Confirmed not religiously affiliated — Drexel has been a non-sectarian private research university since its 1891 founding, explicitly founded with no religious restrictions; no theology/religion course appears anywhere in the 8-course ACE prerequisite list or the 22-course nursing curriculum. (4) JANUARY START: Does NOT exist at Drexel. ACE admits only Fall (September) and Spring cohorts; the Spring cohort's confirmed start (per Drexel's official quarter academic calendar) is March 29, 2027 — about 2.5 months after the applicant's January 2027 target, with application due Jan 15, 2027 and remaining prerequisites due Feb 15, 2027. (5) ADDITIONAL RISK — MID-COHORT SEMESTER CONVERSION: Drexel converts its entire university from quarters to semesters effective August 23, 2027 (with a one-time Summer 2027 transition term, June 21-Aug 7, 2027). The Spring 2027 ACE cohort (Mar 29, 2027 start, 11 months/four 10-week terms, finishing roughly Feb 2028) would hit this conversion mid-program, likely around its second or third term. Drexel's general messaging only promises the conversion 'will not extend time to degree' for students in satisfactory standing and provides no ACE/nursing-specific detail on how curriculum, term structure, or credits will be handled for a cohort literally straddling the changeover — this is a genuinely open, unresolved risk unique to the Spring 2027 cohort that a Fall 2026 or Fall 2027 cohort would not face. (6) GREENLIGHTS: Applicant is otherwise an excellent fit on paper — Drexel's prereq list is comparatively lean (8 courses; no sociology, general biology, ethics, or patho/pharm extras required), no TEAS/HESI exam, and the applicant will have completed all four science prerequisites (Chem, A&P I, A&P II, Micro) well before the Jan 15, 2027 application deadline — exceeding Drexel's own minimum bar of 'A&P plus one of micro/chem done at application, fourth science due by Feb 15.' NCLEX pass rates are strong. Net: Drexel ACE is a well-matched program on prerequisites and cost but fails the applicant's January-start target by ~2.5 months and carries two unresolved risks (online lab acceptance, mid-cohort semester conversion) that should be confirmed directly with admissions before treating it as a top choice. | DURATION/DATES/COST all confirm the previously known data almost exactly: 11-month, four consecutive 10-week quarter terms; Spring cohort start of March 29, 2027 is directly confirmed on Drexel's official quarter academic calendar page ('Spring Quarter 2027 begins Monday, March 29, 2027'); application deadline Jan 15 / prerequisite-and-final-transcript deadline Feb 15 for spring confirmed identically across the main ACE admissions page, the CNHP academic program page, and the Incoming ACE Students page. Tuition 2026-27: $13,728/term x 4 = $54,912 (private flat rate; WI residency has no bearing since Drexel is private). Fees: $4,036 first term + $50 x 3 subsequent terms = $4,186 total, matching prior data. PREREQS (8, no waivers/substitutions): English Composition (3cr), Developmental/Lifespan Psychology (3cr), Human Nutrition (3cr), Statistics (3cr), General Chemistry I w/lab (4cr), Anatomy w/lab (4cr) + Physiology w/lab (4cr) [the A&P sequence], Microbiology w/lab (4cr). Grade of C+ or higher needed for transfer credit; competitive applicants have B or better especially in sciences. GPA: 3.0 overall OR 3.0 in most recent 60 semester credits (this 'last-60' framing is explicitly designed to favor career-changers like this applicant). APPLICATION TIMING RULE: A&P I + A&P II plus one of {micro, chem} (i.e., 3 of the 4 sciences) must be fully completed AT TIME OF APPLICATION; the 4th science and all non-science prereqs may be in-progress and are due by the prereq deadline (Feb 15 spring). Applicant will exceed this bar (all 4 sciences done pre-application). EXAM: TEAS/HESI not required anywhere in official ACE materials — consistent across every source checked; ACE's rationale is that a prior bachelor's degree substitutes for the standardized-test signal. APP SYSTEM: Drexel's own application portal, NOT Common App — an official transfer-instructions page explicitly states 'Nursing Accelerated Career Entry applicants must use Drexel's application, not Common App.' ESSAY/REFERENCES/INTERVIEW/DEPOSIT/APP-FEE: lower confidence than other fields. The $65 fee and 250-650 word personal essay come from Drexel's general transfer-applicant instructions page (which does state ACE uses this same application system), so likely apply, but no ACE-nursing-specific essay prompt was found. The 'no letters of recommendation required' language on that same general transfer page conflicts with several secondary/aggregator sources repeatedly citing '2 letters of recommendation' for ACE nursing specifically — flagging this conflict rather than guessing; treat references_count=2 as moderate- not high-confidence. No interview requirement was found in any source (official or forum/aggregator), so interview='none' but this is an absence-of-evidence call. Deposit figure ($300) is Drexel's general undergraduate non-refundable enrollment deposit, not confirmed as ACE-specific; a separate $200 deposit exists only for students wanting on-campus housing. BACKGROUND CHECK / IMMUNIZATIONS / BLS: A formal compliance process is required post-confirmation of enrollment (background check, clearances); immunization record form due Sept 1 (fall) / Apr 30 (spring) with 'additional immunization requirements' specific to nursing students; AHA BLS certification required per Drexel CNHP continuing-ed pages (standard for nursing clinicals, though not spelled out on the core ACE admissions page itself). Small cohorts (max ~30), interview + personal statement + resume required, 3.0 cumulative / 2.8 science GPA floors. programs.notes: CRITICAL PRELIMINARY FINDING that supersedes the rest of this pass: the 'Philadelphia Center City' ABSN campus (600 Chestnut St) this program entry is named for appears CLOSED, not a currently active distinct site. Per Gwynedd Mercy's official regional accreditor (MSCHE) location record: the Philadelphia Center City location 'relocated' to Bensalem per an Oct 28, 2021 action, and Bensalem itself then 'ceased operations' and was 'closed on December 16, 2022' with teach-out completed May 11, 2024. A Yelp listing independently corroborates '600 Chestnut St., Philadelphia' is closed. Current official GMercyU pages (Our Campuses; ABSN program page; School of Nursing page) make zero mention of Philadelphia/Chestnut/Bensalem and describe the ABSN program as based solely on the Gwynedd Valley, PA campus. So there is no separate Philadelphia-campus cohort to apply to in 2026-27 -- an applicant would be applying to the single Gwynedd Valley-based ABSN program. All data fields describe that program (real, current, CCNE-accredited), not a Philadelphia-specific one. RECOMMEND MERGING/RECONCILING this entry with any existing Gwynedd Valley program entry. EXACT JAN 2027 START DATE: GMercyU's ABSN page only lists 'January 2027 (spring)' as one of three start options (Aug 2026/Jan 2027/May 2027), no day-level date published; general Spring 2027 classes begin January 11, 2027 per the academic calendar, but the calendar explicitly warns 'ABSN and online session sections may have different dates' -- 2027-01-11 is a best estimate, NOT confirmed as the ABSN-specific day. DEADLINE: no explicit deadline date found anywhere despite extensive searching; direct-application (not NursingCAS), 3 start options/year, consistently characterized as rolling admission. ONLINE LAB CRITICAL QUESTION (direct answer): Two separate official GMercyU pages (ABSN program page + dedicated online-prerequisite-courses page) both state in matching language: 'Science courses must have included a lab component, which was completed in the classroom or online with a kit. Virtual labs are not accepted.' I also found an explicit carve-out elsewhere reading 'Virtual labs are accepted for A&P I and II' but confirmed via direct fetch that carve-out lives on the page for traditional first-time-freshman/sophomore-transfer BSN students (under 45 transfer credits), which never mentions ABSN/second-degree students, so it does not clearly extend to this applicant's pathway. Net answer: online_lab_policy = not_accepted for ABSN specifically, WITH the caveat that 'online with a kit' (physical at-home lab materials) may be distinguished from a purely virtual/simulated lab -- the applicant should confirm with admissions (833-588-5953 / accelerate@gmercyu.edu) exactly what lab format her A&P I/II courses used before ruling this program in or out. | TUITION: $49,044 reconfirmed directly on the official tuition page: ABSN coursework billed at $732/credit x 67 credits = $49,044 exactly. FEES: fees_total ($4,397) is my sum of individually-published official fee line items (comprehensive fee $725/semester x4 + ATI learning systems $875 + ExamSoft $80 + Hurst Review NCLEX prep $279 + nursing kit $88 + graduation fee $175) -- GMercyU does not publish one single 'total fees' figure, so treat as approximate. Explicitly EXCLUDED from fees_total: the $500 acceptance deposit (reported separately) and a $225-300 compliance/immunization-management fee paid directly to a third-party vendor. PREREQ RECENCY: science prereqs (chemistry, A&P I/II, microbiology, nutrition) must be completed within 7 years of admission; statistics and lifespan/developmental psychology within 10 years -- applicant's coursework is all 2026, clears either window comfortably. IN-PROGRESS PREREQS: official language is 'you do not need to have your prerequisites completed before you apply, but... at least four science prerequisite courses [must be complete] before an admissions decision can be made' and 'all prerequisite courses must be successfully completed prior to starting the program.' Applicant already has 4 of 5 science prereqs done (chemistry, A&P I, A&P II, nutrition) with microbiology finishing Aug 1, 2026 -- should already satisfy the 4-course threshold well ahead of a January 2027 start. NUTRITION INSTRUCTOR RULE: official pages specifically require the Nutrition prerequisite to be 'taught by a Registered Dietitian' -- worth double-checking the applicant's completed Nutrition course instructor's credentials. NCLEX: 91.39% first-time pass rate for 2023, described as 'highest in program history,' beating PA state average (90.70%) and national average (86.73%) -- this figure is for GMercyU's BSN program generally, could not confirm broken out separately for ABSN or the now-closed Philadelphia site. THEOLOGY: no explicit statement found either requiring or waiving theology coursework in the ABSN track; inferred required_coursework=false because every curriculum description of the 67-credit ABSN sequence found lists only nursing/science/professional content with no gen-ed or theology course ever named. RESIDENCY: private university with a single flat tuition rate; no in-state/OOS distinction applies. UNCONFIRMED DESPITE REAL EFFORT: references/recommendation-letter count, personal-statement word range, and stated interview policy were not found on any official admissions-requirements page -- interview reported as 'none' with only moderate confidence. The $0 application fee is based on search-engine synthesis of official-page language, not independently re-confirmed via direct fetch. Recommend the applicant email accelerate@gmercyu.edu or call 833-588-5953 to nail down exact start date/deadline, the online-lab-kit question, references/essay/interview specifics, and confirm Gwynedd Valley is truly the only remaining site.

programs.notes: PreSpecialty MSN entry: NOT possible in January. Confirmed via the official MN program page that MN Prespecialty admits FALL ONLY (to preserve continuity into the specialty program); only the MN Generalist track admits both Jan and Aug, so a Jan 11, 2027 start requires applying Generalist, not Prespecialty. That means the 'seamless' transition into an NP specialty is not available on the Jan timeline -- a Generalist-track grad would need to apply separately/later to a post-master's specialty. Current deadlines: Spring 2027 priority review was May 15, 2026 (passed). This is a SOFT priority deadline, not a hard cutoff -- Vanderbilt's own admissions FAQ states applications are welcomed on a rolling basis after the priority date until the cohort fills, so applying now (mid-July) is still plausible but likely disadvantaged for scholarship funding and seat availability; call admissions (615-322-3800) to confirm remaining Jan 2027 capacity before investing in an application. Prespecialty-year cost: moot for the Jan 2027 target since Prespecialty isn't offered then; if pursued later (Fall entry), the same $2,057/credit rate applies to the 3-4 additional specialty semesters, but the specific credit count depends on which specialty is chosen (not published in one place). Online A&P labs: ACCEPTED with good confidence -- Vanderbilt's own prerequisite program (explicitly marketed as a feeder into its own MN admissions) delivers A&P I, A&P II, and microbiology entirely online, stating lab activities 'are completed online through the learning platform and do not require in-person attendance.' No source suggests they'd reject equivalent online labs completed elsewhere, and general nursing-admissions framing everywhere emphasizes institutional accreditation over delivery format. No explicit written 'we accept 3rd-party online A&P labs' policy was found, so this isn't 100% ironclad, but it is the strongest positive signal of any of the 4 programs vetted in this batch. | Of the 4 programs in this batch, Vanderbilt MN Generalist is the best prereq match for this applicant: no chemistry requirement at all (unusual -- confirmed absent from every prereq list found), and A&P/micro/stats/lifespan/nutrition are all satisfied by the applicant's 2026 coursework (microbio in-progress is fine since Vanderbilt only requires prereqs complete 'by the time classes begin,' not at application time). programs.notes: Online A&P lab: no single Bushnell page states outright that online labs are accepted, but the official ABSN FAQ explicitly approves 'accredited independent providers like Portage Learning' as a valid prerequisite source in the very same answer that excludes Sophia Learning/StraighterLine on accreditation grounds -- and Portage Learning's A&P I/II courses are independently confirmed to use fully virtual labs/simulations with no physical kit, i.e. the same 'online lab' modality the applicant used. That is coded here as 'accepted' on strong circumstantial evidence, not a direct quote -- get it in writing via Bushnell's free transcript evaluation (online@bushnell.edu) before relying on it. Recency: Bushnell uses a two-tier, calendar-year window (7 years for Biology/A&P/Microbiology, 10 years for Nutrition/Human Growth & Development, counted to the cohort's start year), so all of the applicant's 2026 coursework clears comfortably while the 2001-2005 UW-Madison-era coursework is uniformly too old to count for anything at Bushnell. However, Bushnell also requires a standalone Biology (cell/molecular/genetics) course separate from A&P that does not appear anywhere in the applicant's listed 2026 coursework -- a real gap to resolve before applying. Religious: Bushnell is Disciples of Christ/Stone-Campbell-heritage Christian (formerly Northwest Christian University); its FAQ states Bible/theology coursework is required only for ABSN students using the program as their FIRST bachelor's degree, so the applicant (already holding a UW-Madison bachelor's) should be exempt from a theology course -- but campus life is still meaningfully faith-infused (daily 'Christian worldview' exposure is explicitly flagged to applicants, nursing coursework includes scripture-based 'nursing as calling' assignments, and 'faith journey' is literally a scored criterion on the required admissions essay), so this remains a genuine culture-fit question even with no mandatory class. The single biggest red flag found, independent of the two target questions: a current CNA certification or LPN/LVN license is required of every ABSN applicant with no coursework substitute, called 'non-negotiable' by admissions -- the applicant does not hold one and cannot obtain one before January 2027, making this a likely hard blocker despite the otherwise strong timing fit. Green lights: no TEAS/HESI exam, in-progress coursework explicitly permitted, the Sep 1 2026 deadline lands safely after the Aug 1 2026 microbiology grade, GPA minimum (2.75 for prior-degree holders) is modest, and NCLEX first-time pass rates have been 100% four years running. | TUITION/DATES: Confirmed via the official ABSN page: 44 credits x $1,225/credit = $53,900 flat tuition (private school, no in-state/OOS distinction). fees_total=$2,050 reflects the published 'Student Fees' line items across all 3 semesters ($1,650 sem1 + $400 sem2 + $0 sem3); this EXCLUDES a separate ~$175/semester Tech Fee and EXCLUDES cost-of-attendance estimates for housing/food (~$5,650/sem), personal (~$700/sem), transportation (~$700/sem), and books (~$525/sem), which are living-cost estimates rather than mandatory institutional fees. Two cohorts/year: Fall (Aug start, Apr 1 deadline) and Spring (Jan start, Sep 1 deadline) -- Sep 1, 2026 deadline reconfirmed on two separate official pages. FAQ states 'students who start in January graduate in December of the same calendar year,' which reads closer to ~11 months than a full 12 for the Spring cohort specifically -- worth confirming exact Jan start day/Dec 2027 end date with admissions (the Jan 15 start day carried over from prior data was not independently reverified; only 'January' is confirmed in current sources). ONLINE LAB POLICY: see open_question_answers for the full reasoning chain; no explicit sentence exists in the prerequisite checklist PDFs (2021 and 2022 versions), prerequisite-courses webpage, admission-requirements webpage, full FAQ page/PDF, or 2025-26 catalog. RECENCY: catalog language is precise -- '7 and 10 years are measured from the calendar year that the prerequisite was taken to the calendar year that the cohort begins,' e.g. for a cohort starting in 2023 science prereqs must be from 2016+ and nutrition/human-growth-and-development from 2013+. Applying that formula to a 2027 cohort: science courses need to be from calendar-year 2020 or later, nutrition/human-growth-and-development from 2017 or later. RELIGIOUS: a separate catalog passage about general 'block transfer' degree evaluation says block-transferred degrees satisfy gen-ed 'except Bible' -- this may reflect a different, university-wide transfer policy rather than the ABSN-specific second-degree track; the direct ABSN FAQ answer ('ABSN students pursuing their first bachelor's degree must take Biblical studies') is treated as controlling here since it addresses the ABSN program by name, but this conflict is worth having the applicant confirm in writing. OTHER: GPA is a three-tier system per the current admission-requirements page and 2025-26 catalog -- 2.75 for applicants who already hold a bachelor's degree (applicant's situation), 3.0 for applicants using ABSN as a first bachelor's degree, and 3.25 for current Bushnell students transferring internally into ABSN. The $21,000 Nursing Tuition Grant is NOT a standard/automatic award: it is funded via a Lane Community Health Council partnership, requires a completed FAFSA or ORSAA, and prioritizes applicants self-identifying as from communities of color, from underserved communities, or intending culturally-responsive/Lane-County-focused practice; its priority deadline for the Fall 2026 cohort was July 1, 2026 (already past as of this research), and no Spring-2027-specific deadline was found in any source -- ask admissions directly whether a parallel window exists and whether the applicant's profile fits the stated priority criteria before counting on this money. Cohort size is 'up to 32 students' per the current live FAQ page (expanded from an original cap of 16 following Oregon State Board of Nursing approval in April 2023); treat 32 as current. NCLEX-RN first-time pass rate has been 100% every year 2022-2025 (33 candidates in 2025), and the program was named best in Oregon in a Sept 2025 Bushnell news release. Application fee amount could not be found in any source; the ABSN application routes through NursingCAS (confirmed via the 2025-26 catalog: 'Completed application through NursingCAS'), so NursingCAS's standard fee schedule plus any Bushnell-specific supplemental fee would apply -- check the live NursingCAS Bushnell program listing directly, since Bushnell's own DIRECT undergraduate application (unrelated to NursingCAS) is advertised elsewhere as fee-free. Exam: none required (no TEAS/HESI/Kaplan). absnprograms.org (a third-party lead-generation site) was used only as light corroboration, never as a primary source.

programs.notes: ONLINE A&P LAB: Genuinely UNKNOWN despite an exhaustive search — fetched the official ABSN Pre-Requisites PDF, the ABSN Application PDF, the BSN Student Handbook (2024-2025), the Pre-Licensure and ABSN program pages, the Registrar's transfer-credit policy page, and a Nursing Curriculum Planning Guide, plus multiple targeted searches for Labster/virtual-lab language. All confirm a lab component is required (BIOL 230L, BIOL 240L) but NONE state whether the lab must be in-person/on-campus or whether an online/virtual lab is acceptable. This must be confirmed directly with the nursing advisor (Josephine Moore, jsmoore@uncfsu.edu) before relying on this program. RECENCY: Confirmed explicitly — 'All math and science prerequisite courses must be taken within a five (5) year period from the date of application,' effective January 18, 2025. This applies ONLY to math/science courses. The applicant's 2026 science coursework (Chem, A&P I/II, Microbiology) is comfortably within the window; the 2001-2005 coursework would be stale for any math/science course but the recency cap does NOT apply to non-science gen-eds (English, Sociology, Psychology, Speech, Philosophy), which could potentially still count from that era if equivalent and transferable — a real advantage of this program's narrower recency rule. RELIGIOUS: Confirmed NOT religiously affiliated — FSU is a public HBCU in the UNC System (founded 1867), and no religion/theology coursework appears anywhere in the nursing curriculum (PHIL 110/220 is Critical Thinking/Logic, not theology). JANUARY START: CONFIRMED there is no January 2027 start. The Jan 1-17, 2027 window is only the APPLICATION period; the cohort itself begins the following Maymester (~mid-May 2027), roughly 4 months after the applicant's target. This is a firm scheduling mismatch, not a data error. | TUITION CORRECTION: The prior $291.67/credit figure appears to have been a misread. Official Fall2025-Spring2026 tuition schedules (fetched via uncfsu.edu/a/19910 for Main Campus and /a/19911 for Distance Ed) show $41.67/credit is the NC-RESIDENT rate ($41.67x7=$291.69, which likely produced the earlier $291.67 figure); the actual OUT-OF-STATE Main Campus rate is $208.34/credit, or a flat $2,500.00/semester cap at 12+ credits, PLUS mandatory fees of $1,706.00/semester for non-residents (itemized: athletic, student activity, health services, debt service, ed & tech, security, Bronco Card, digital book access — verified line-by-line, sums correctly to $1,706). A separate, lower Distance-Education-only OOS schedule also exists ($104.17/credit, $1,250/semester cap + ~$599 fees) — could NOT confirm whether FSU bills its hybrid ABSN track under Main Campus or Distance Ed rates; given the program includes on-campus simulation and live clinical rotations, Main Campus billing is more likely, so the higher, more conservative schedule was used. CREDIT COUNT: Triangulated ~60-61 nursing-major credit hours from two independent sources (absnprograms.org: '60 nursing credit hours'; FSU Registrar's Nursing Generic Curriculum Planning Guide: '61 upper division nursing courses' within a 127-credit total 4-year plan). Used 61. tuition_total = 61 credits x $208.34 = $12,709 (tuition only, OOS — applicant is a WI resident; NC public school). fees_total = 4 semesters x $1,706 = $6,824 (assumed 4 billed full-time terms across the 16-month span; could be 5 terms if Maymester bills as a separate term, which would push fees toward ~$8,530). Combined tuition+fees estimate: roughly $19,500-21,200 OOS, BEFORE typical nursing ancillary costs (background check, drug screen, immunizations, uniforms, liability insurance, Kaplan exam fee — not itemized anywhere accessible, commonly $1,000-2,500 industry-wide). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: FSU's Cost-of-Attendance budget page shows OOS tuition rising to a '$5,000-$7,000' annual RANGE for 2026-27 (vs. the $5,000/year used, which is the confirmed 2025-26 rate) — likely reflecting UNC System's multi-year tuition-guarantee cohort structure where NEW incoming students may lock in a higher rate than continuing students. Could not access a working 2026-27 or 2027-28 detailed rate table (several official PDFs on uncfsu.edu are scanned/image-only and would not parse even via a text-extraction proxy), so this tuition estimate could be a meaningful UNDERCOUNT for a 2027 entrant — verify current rates directly with the Bursar. DURATION: 16 months (May 2027 Maymester start through program completion; supersedes prior 15-month figure). KAPLAN EXAM: Confirmed still required and current (found in both the 2024-updated ABSN Application PDF and multiple program pages) — minimum score 65, maximum 2 attempts total, only 1 attempt per semester, taken AFTER application submission, proctored by the University Testing Center. GPA: 3.0 minimum specifically on math/science prerequisite GPA (also stated as overall undergrad GPA >=3.0); separately, 2.0 overall GPA required for graduation (not admission). NCLEX: Official NC Board of Nursing 2025 single-year first-time pass-rate document (fetched directly) shows Fayetteville State University BSN at 98% — explicitly disambiguated from Fayetteville TECHNICAL COMMUNITY COLLEGE's separate ADN program (also 98% that year, coincidentally, in the same document). A separate, less-clearly-sourced secondary search suggested a 3-year (2022-2024) trend of 78%/84%/96% with an ~86% average, consistent with normal small-cohort year-to-year volatility — the 98% (2025) official BON figure is the most trusted. STATS/NUTRITION: Notably, FSU's official ABSN Pre-Requisites PDF does NOT list a standalone Statistics or Nutrition course requirement (math requirement is College Algebra/Quantitative Reasoning, not Statistics) — unusual versus most nursing programs; non-issue for the applicant either way. SECOND-DEGREE WAIVERS: Many listed 'prerequisites' (UNIV 101/102 seminars, ENGL 110/120, CSC 100, PE/Wellness, and per explicit document language ETCE 101 and PHIL 110/220) look like a first-time-freshman gen-ed path; the source document explicitly states transfer students with 60+ credit hours are exempt from ETCE 101 and PHIL — the applicant, holding a full bachelor's degree, likely qualifies for broader gen-ed waivers, but no FSU-specific 'second bachelor's degree' blanket waiver policy was found to confirm this beyond that one explicit exemption — recommend confirming a personalized required list directly with Ms. Josephine Moore (jsmoore@uncfsu.edu), the ABSN admissions contact. APPLICATION FEE: The $50 non-refundable fee found is FSU's general undergraduate application fee (required since ABSN applicants must first be admitted to FSU as a university student); the ABSN-specific Application PDF itself lists no additional separate nursing-program application fee, but one could not be 100% ruled out. DEPOSIT: No enrollment deposit requirement found in any accessible document — likely none beyond a possible ~$165 orientation fee found in the general fee schedule, but unconfirmed as nursing-specific. RESIDENCY: No residency restriction on admission found — FSU publishes standard non-resident tuition rates confirming it accepts OOS applicants; as a Wisconsin resident, the applicant would pay out-of-state rates (Texas residency plans are irrelevant here since NC governs this program's in-state/OOS line). METHODOLOGY NOTE: Most of uncfsu.edu's official nursing PDFs are scanned/image-based and would not parse via direct fetch; text was extracted via a web-based text-extraction proxy (r.jina.ai) as a read-only pass-through of the same public URLs.

programs.notes: RESIDENCY: No Michigan-residency admission restriction found. Non-Michigan applicants are eligible and pay the nonresident upper-division rate; no Michigan-Wisconsin reciprocity was found. | (1) Aug 1-8 window: CONFIRMED exact and real via GVSU KCON's own official 'Second Degree B.S.N. Curriculum Checklist and Admissions Criteria' PDF (Catalog Year Fall 2025 or after), the single most authoritative source found: 'Complete an Application August 1-8 for admission into the winter semester (January).' Opens 8:00am Aug 1, closes 5:00pm Aug 8, no late applications, not rolling. (2) Can patho/pharm/chem be done fall 2026? THIS IS THE CRITICAL FINDING: GVSU splits prerequisites into two tiers with DIFFERENT timing rules, and the scout data mischaracterized them. TIER 1 'Admission Prerequisites' (21cr: BIO 355 Human Genetics, BMS 212 Microbiology, BMS 250/251 A&P I/II, CHM 234 Introductory Biochemistry, PSY 364 Lifespan Psych) must be 100% COMPLETE with a posted grade BEFORE submitting the Aug 1-8 application -- NOT in-progress-ok, NOT deferrable to fall 2026. TIER 2 'additional courses' (9cr: BMS 305 Clinical Nutrition, BMS 310 Pathophysiology, STA 215 Statistics) CAN be in-progress at application time, just must finish before the Jan 2027 start. So: Pathophysiology (BMS 310) CAN be added fall 2026 -- good, since applicant lacks it. But there is NO pharmacology prerequisite in this program at all -- NUR 326 'Nursing Pharmacology' is a course TAKEN DURING the program (semester 1), not a pre-admission requirement. The scout's 'patho/pharm (BMS 305/310)' was wrong on two counts: BMS 305 is actually Clinical Nutrition (applicant already has equivalent coursework) and BMS 310 is Pathophysiology (singular, not patho+pharm). More importantly, 'GVSU-chem' (CHM 234) is a TIER-1 admission prerequisite -- it must be done BEFORE Aug 1-8, 2026, not fall 2026. CHM 234 is titled 'Introductory Biochemistry' with its own prerequisite of CHM 109 (i.e., it is a second/follow-on chemistry course, not entry-level general chemistry). The applicant's completed 'General Chemistry (with in-person lab)' is very unlikely to be accepted as equivalent to a biochemistry course -- these are different course content. Combined with BIO 355 Human Genetics (also Tier-1, also not in the applicant's stated coursework), the applicant appears to have TWO unresolved Tier-1 gaps that cannot legally be deferred past Aug 1-8, 2026 under this program's own rules, and essentially no time remains to newly complete either course before the window opens. A THIRD, narrower risk: her Microbiology (also Tier-1) completes Aug 1, 2026 -- the FIRST day of the window -- creating real risk that an official posted grade/updated transcript won't reach GVSU Admissions within the 8-day application period. Bottom line: unless she already holds transferable genetics and biochemistry credit not mentioned in her profile, or GVSU's transfer-equivalency process credits her existing coursework for these two specific courses, this cycle is very likely not reachable, and she should verify this with KCON immediately rather than waiting. (3) Online A&P labs: marked UNKNOWN -- no explicit public policy found either accepting or rejecting online-lab transfer credit for the BMS 250/251 (A&P I/II) equivalency. Circumstantial (not conclusive) signal: among all prerequisite courses, GVSU states only STA 215 is offered online/hybrid at GVSU itself -- BMS 250/251 are not offered online there, suggesting an in-person-lab institutional norm, but this describes GVSU's own course delivery, not their transfer-acceptance rule for a course completed online elsewhere. GVSU's transfer process runs through a Course Equivalency Guide (gvsu.edu/studentapps/mtn) for previously-evaluated courses, or a Registrar equivalency-appeal (submit transcript + syllabus) for anything not already listed -- this is NOT instant, and there is no stated guarantee it completes within the Aug 1-8 window if not already resolved beforehand. Given two other unresolved prerequisite gaps already make this cycle doubtful, the online-lab question is somewhat moot near-term, but if she pursues a future cycle she should submit her A&P transcripts for equivalency evaluation (including asking explicitly and in writing whether the online lab component is acceptable) well in advance of any future application window, since no public GVSU document resolves this either way. | SEATS/COMPETITIVENESS: Official PDF confirms 48 students admitted per cohort (fall/winter/summer each) -- corrects scout's '24 seats.' GPA floor is 2.70 overall AND 2.70 prerequisite-only (both include non-GVSU coursework), min grade 'C' not C- in every prerequisite course; admitted students' GPAs have ranged 2.70-4.0 per KCON's own application-prep page, but a separate KCON FAQ states interviews go to applicants meeting '3.0 overall and 3.0 prerequisite GPA' eligibility -- so while 2.70 is the hard floor to apply, competitive/practical footing is closer to 3.0+. ADMISSION PROCESS: 4 balanced components, ~25% each: prerequisite GPA, interview (in-person, DeVos Center, 15 min, 5 behavioral/reflective questions, offered to all who clear eligibility ~1 month after the window closes), personal statement (650-word open response), and a 'Student Profile' (structured, non-essay: work/leadership/study-abroad/health-care-shadow/certifications/languages/volunteer experience with reflection -- second-degree version asks for more depth than the traditional-track version). No letters of recommendation found anywhere in the official checklist or FAQs -- set references_count=0 rather than null since the source is thorough and simply doesn't include them. No NursingCAS use found anywhere -- this is a fully DIRECT/internal GVSU application. app_fee=30 reflects GVSU's standard undergraduate application fee (charged once, for the prerequisite general-university admission step below) -- no separate fee was found for the KCON secondary nursing application itself. HIDDEN EARLIER DEADLINE (directive #5): Per the official PDF, 'Students must be admitted as degree-seeking undergraduate students for the semester in which they intend to begin the professional nursing program' AND must 'Declare Nursing major prior to secondary application submission.' A separate KCON program page phrases this as needed 'no later than the semester preceding the start... the application deadline to GVSU... will be during the fall semester.' Regardless of exact phrasing, the operative fact is unambiguous: she must already be an admitted, nursing-major-declared, degree-seeking GVSU undergrad BEFORE she can submit the Aug 1-8 nursing application. GVSU's general undergrad/second-bachelor's admission is rolling ('at least 30 days before the final day of registration... subject to earlier closing without notice'), with GVSU stating ~3-week typical turnaround -- no fixed Fall-2026 hard deadline was publicly found, but given the ~2-3 weeks remaining before Aug 1, this general-admission step is urgent and should be started immediately if not already done, independent of the prerequisite-course gaps above. TUITION MATH: Scout data assumed a 33-credit professional sequence; GVSU's own official curriculum-checklist PDF instead itemizes 53-55 credits of NUR/IPE coursework across 4 semesters (Sem1=14cr, Sem2=14.5cr [or 12.5cr if NUR356 substituted], Sem3=13.5cr, Sem4=13cr) -- I verified this by summing every listed course's credits myself. All 4 semesters fall inside GVSU's 12-15-credit 'flat-rate' band, so tuition bills at the flat per-semester rate, not itemized per-credit. Confirmed 2026-27 official rates (gvsu.edu/financialaid): non-resident upper-division flat semester = $12,092; MI-resident upper-division flat semester = $8,626 (upper-division applies because second-degree students already hold 120+ credits from their first bachelor's). Per this database's tuition rule (in-state rates only for WI/TX public schools; GVSU is a MI public school so OOS applies), non-resident total = $12,092 x 4 = $48,368 -- this is my own derivation, shown for transparency. It EXCLUDES an unquantified 'additional tuition charge per credit hour for 300-level-and-above NUR courses' that GVSU mentions exists but does not publicly itemize anywhere I could find, plus GVSU's mandatory per-semester general fee (amount not found), plus supplies (uniform, stethoscope, BP cuff) and background-check/drug-screen/immunization costs -- so treat $48,368 as a FLOOR, true cost is somewhat higher. A different total ($43,788 non-resident / $31,004 resident, 'four semesters') recurs across several secondary/aggregator sources (e.g. absnprograms.org), but that source itself states it could not confirm per-credit rates and directs readers to verify with GVSU directly, and I could not independently reconcile it against verified official rates and the verified credit structure using any consistent methodology (flat-rate or per-credit, at either 25-26 or 26-27 pricing) -- it may be stale. Recommend applicant get a direct written quote from GVSU Student Accounts/One Stop before relying on either figure. In-state ($727/credit, $8,626/semester flat) is about 71% of non-resident cost, NOT 'half' as scout data assumed. No Michigan-Wisconsin tuition reciprocity found -- Michigan is not among the 8 Midwest Student Exchange Program (MSEP) member states (Indiana, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, Wisconsin), so full non-resident rate applies with no discount avenue identified. NCLEX: GVSU's own site only makes a qualitative claim ('consistently above state and national average'), with the only dated data point found referencing a 2018-2019 assessment-report snippet (no current percentage). Third-party aggregators (rncareers.org: 92.31% over an unspecified 3-year window; nursingschoolsalmanac-derived search snippet: 93.27%/90%, years unclear) cluster in the low-to-mid 90s but are not primary-sourced or consistently dated, and I could not access the Michigan LARA official NCLEX score-summary PDF directly (blocked, 403) to independently confirm -- left as null per instructions rather than guessing a specific rate+year. POST-ADMISSION COMPLIANCE (not required at application): physical exam, immunization verification (Rubella, Rubeola, Polio, DPT, TB, Hep B, flu shot, MMR/Hep B/Varicella titers), criminal background check + drug screen through a KCON-specified vendor, and annual AHA CPR/BLS certification -- all required of SELECTED/admitted students only, before program start, not part of the application itself. No enrollment deposit amount/timing was found in any official source despite a fairly thorough search, including the authoritative PDF checklist which otherwise itemizes compliance items in detail -- left null. Program is CCNE-accredited and Michigan-Board-of-Nursing-approved; face-to-face format at the DeVos Center for Interprofessional Health in downtown Grand Rapids ('hybrid' language on some pages likely refers to some prerequisite/gen-ed delivery, not the professional nursing sequence itself, which is explicitly 'face to face').
