programs.notes: RESIDENCY: No admissions residency restriction found; regional residency is only an admissions consideration. For tuition, Texas A&M ordinarily requires 12 consecutive months of physical residence and domicile before the census date. The applicant has longstanding Texas mailing-address and utility evidence tha | HESI A2 timing: YES, realistically feasible before the Aug 1, 2026 deadline. The College of Nursing has a direct partnership with Elsevier HESI + ProctorU for secure ONLINE PROCTORED testing (no physical testing-center seat required); scores taken through that TAMU-partnered pathway are 'available electronically within 24 hours of the date of the exam' with no separate score-request step. Given ~2.5 weeks of runway from today, she should set up her Evolve account and schedule a ProctorU slot immediately. AVOID the alternate route of testing through a different institution/testing center and requesting a transferred score report — the same official page warns that path 'can take up to two weeks for the college to receive your scores.' Minimum 75% is required in EACH of 5 sections (Math, Reading Comprehension, Vocabulary & General Knowledge, Grammar, Anatomy & Physiology); max 2 attempts per rolling 12-month period; the exam must have been taken within 12 months of the application deadline. TX core burden for out-of-state degree holders: CONFIRMED as real, not a false assumption in the scout data. The official admissions page states plainly: 'Applicants from out-of-state or private universities must complete courses that are Texas A&M core equivalent.' A softer-sounding line in the course catalog ('core curriculum requirements if these were not met in the previous degree program') is scoped to students who already hold a TAMU-conferred degree, not out-of-state degree holders generally — so a prior Wisconsin bachelor's degree does not create a blanket exemption; TAMU does a course-by-course 'core equivalent' evaluation of the prior transcript at time of application. In practice the sharpest edge is TEXAS GOVERNMENT (POLS 207/GOVT 2306), a Texas-specific course essentially impossible to have satisfied out of state; Federal Government, Communications (x2), American History (x2), Creative Arts, Philosophy/Ethics, and Math may or may not already be covered by her UW-Madison coursework pending TAMU's equivalency review. The good news: none of this gen-ed/core coursework has to be finished by the Aug 1 deadline, only by the first day of nursing classes roughly five months later, so it's a real but schedulable burden (e.g., an online/community-college TX Government course over fall 2026), not a same-day dealbreaker. | DURATION: nursing.tamu.edu states 'a 15-month, four-semester accelerated program' (stated twice on the official admissions page, matching scout data); catalog.tamu.edu's overview blurb instead says 'graduating in just 16 months' for the same track — a minor discrepancy between two official TAMU sources, likely imprecise rounding either way; going with 15 months as primary since the dedicated program page is more authoritative and consistent. START DATE: the official nursing admissions 'Dates and Deadlines' section lists Spring Entry orientation as 'NSC: TBD, NSO: TBD' as of this research — the nursing program's own Spring 2027 cohort start date is not yet published. The official TAMU Registrar Spring 2027 academic calendar (catalog.tamu.edu/undergraduate/academic-calendar/academic-calendar.pdf) states unambiguously 'January 19 [2027] Tuesday. First day of spring semester classes' for the general College Station calendar, and the same calendar's only Nursing-specific carve-outs are day-level exceptions (redefined days, reading day) rather than a wholesale different start date — suggesting nursing follows the general semester start. I am reporting 2027-01-19 (not the scout's 2027-01-11, which I could not verify against any source) but this should be confirmed once Round Rock orientation dates are published; nursingadmissions@tamu.edu can confirm. MICROBIOLOGY FINISHING SAME-DAY AS DEADLINE (Directive #4): the official page separates two different deadlines. General rule: 'Courses may be in progress during the application cycle; however, all courses must be completed with a minimum grade of C by the first class day' — i.e., the hard completion deadline for ALL 59 prereq hours (including microbiology) is the first day of nursing classes (~5 months after Aug 1), not Aug 1 itself. Narrower sub-rule for the Aug 1 deadline itself: 'By the application deadline, applicants must have completed a minimum of 40 prerequisite course credit hours of the 59 hours required. Of those 40, 12 credit hours must be from the following nursing science courses: General psychology, lifespan psychology, statistics, chemistry, anatomy and physiology, and microbiology.' A companion TAMU Nutrition Dept transfer-planning PDF phrases the same rule more clearly as a 12-hour MINIMUM subset ('12 hours of those 40 must be from the Nursing Science prerequisites of...'), not a requirement that all ~25 hours of that course list be done. The applicant's already-completed 2026 coursework (Chemistry-with-lab 4cr + A&P I 4cr + A&P II 4cr + Statistics 3cr + Lifespan Psych 3cr + Nutrition 3cr = 21 credit hours, all A grades) already clears the 12-hour nursing-science sub-minimum on its own, with no need for Microbiology to be graded by Aug 1. The remaining open question is whether she can document ~19 more prerequisite/gen-ed credit hours (from anywhere in the 59-hour list, likely her original 2001-2005/2020-conferred UW-Madison bachelor's degree gen-ed coursework) to clear the 40-total-hour floor by Aug 1 — a full bachelor's degree very plausibly covers this, but isn't confirmed here. Recommend applying by Aug 1 showing microbiology as 'in progress, completing 8/1/2026' and confirming this reading directly with nursingadmissions@tamu.edu given the stakes. ONLINE A&P LAB POLICY (CRITICAL ISSUE) — marked 'unknown' per instructions: extensive searching of nursing.tamu.edu (admissions + compliance pages), the 2026-2027 catalog, and TAMU-affiliated prereq-planning PDFs (Nutrition Dept guide, pre-req planner) found NO explicit TAMU-specific statement accepting or rejecting online-format A&P labs. The single closest piece of language, from the TAMU Nutrition Department's own official prerequisite/transfer guide, is generic advisory caution, not a stated TAMU policy: 'If taking science courses at a community college, it is safest to complete the lab in person, as some nursing programs do not accept online labs.' This flags the risk category without resolving it for TAMU specifically. Given this is a potential hard-blocker for the applicant (both A&P I and A&P II labs were online), she should email nursingadmissions@tamu.edu directly before Aug 1 and get an explicit yes/no on whether online-format labs satisfy the BIOL 2401/2402-equivalent requirement. TUITION (2026-07-15 AUDIT CORRECTION): Model this January 2027 cohort as OUT-OF-STATE unless and until a Texas residency officer issues a favorable classification. The structured staging total is $61,000, the established project OOS planning estimate. Texas A&M’s official live calculator publishes bundled tuition-and-fee rates rather than a clean four-term program total; applying its current nonresident HSC undergraduate tables to the 61-credit spring-entry sequence gives a substantially higher provisional billed-cost signal of about $83,217 using Fall/Spring 2026-27 and Summer 2026 proxy rates. Summer 2027, Fall 2027, and Spring 2028 rates are not all published, so neither figure is a quote. Treat $61,000 as a planning floor and obtain a written four-term Round Rock estimate from Aggie One Stop/Student Business Services. RESIDENCY/COST REALISM FLAG: The applicant may present longstanding Texas mailing-address and utility evidence, but the official test examines 12 consecutive months of physical residence and domicile and no favorable ruling exists. Keep OOS for the whole sequence unless the State Policies Team decides otherwise. APPLICATION SYSTEM/FEE (2026-07-15 AUDIT CORRECTION): NursingCAS is the program application. Eligible external applicants then receive access to Texas A&M AIS and must pay the separate institutional fee before review; the current College of Nursing page does not instruct applicants to file a second ApplyTexas application. app_system=both reflects NursingCAS plus the required institutional/AIS step, not two duplicative program applications. The combined $145 remains an estimate based on $70 NursingCAS plus $75 institutional fees and should be checked in the live portals. REFERENCES/DEPOSIT: the official admissions page's complete 'To apply, submit your' checklist lists only the NursingCAS application with official transcripts, the HESI A2 score report, the Kira Talent online verbal/written assessment, and international credentials if applicable — letters of recommendation/references are NOT listed anywhere in official TAMU sources reviewed; treat any secondary-source claim that references are required with skepticism. No enrollment/seat deposit amount or policy was found in any official source (Texas public universities often do not charge one the way many private nursing schools do, but this is unconfirmed either way) — recommend confirming directly if admitted. GPA: 3.0 minimum required for BOTH nursing-science GPA and prerequisite GPA, confirmed identically across three independent official/semi-official TAMU documents (admissions page, official pre-req-planner.pdf, Nutrition Dept transfer guide). The Nutrition Dept guide separately notes a 3.5+ prerequisite GPA is recommended to be competitive (not a hard floor). A third-party aggregator's claim of a 3.3 minimum is not corroborated anywhere official and should be disregarded. HESI SCORE MINIMUM: 75% required in each of 5 sections (Math, Reading Comprehension, Vocabulary & General Knowledge, Grammar, Anatomy & Physiology); applicants who miss the minimum in any one section are denied outright based on test-score deficiency; max 2 attempts within the 12 months preceding the deadline, no mandatory waiting period between attempts. NCLEX: Texas A&M College of Nursing's overall first-time NCLEX-RN pass rate was 99.6% in 2025 (250 test-takers), per Texas A&M's own 'Vital Record' news article citing the Texas Board of Nursing's April 2025 pass-rate report (state average 88.63%, national average 86.71% that year); the college's own printed fact sheet separately cites a rounder 'NCLEX pass rate: 99%.' This figure is COLLEGE-WIDE across Bryan-College Station, Round Rock, and McAllen combined — no Round-Rock-specific breakout is published, though the article notes Round Rock's growth is a driver of the college's projected increase from 250 to 450 eligible graduates over the next two years. PSYCH PREREQ GAP FLAG (applicant-specific, not a program-data question but directly relevant): TAMU requires BOTH 'General Psychology' (PSYC 2301/PBSI 107, 3cr) AND 'Developmental Lifespan Psychology' (PSYC 2314/PBSI 225, 3cr) as two SEPARATE nursing-science prerequisites. The applicant's profile lists only 'Lifespan/Developmental Psychology' as completed in 2026, with no separate Intro/General Psychology course mentioned — she should check whether her original 2001-2005 UW-Madison coursework included a general psych course, since TAMU appears to treat these as two distinct required courses, not interchangeable names for one class. DUPLICATE-CAMPUS NOTE: the College of Nursing also offers a Traditional BSN at Bryan-College Station and McAllen; per the official page, 'Applicants may only apply for one program for each application cycle,' and 'Due to strict regulations from the Texas Board of Nursing which govern clinical rotations, the College of Nursing does not allow students to transfer from one campus to another' once enrolled. [MERGE-TIME FIX: interview changed from 'by_invitation' to 'required' — this agent's own research found the Kira Talent online verbal/written assessment listed as a standard, non-optional component of the official 'to apply, submit your...' checklist alongside NursingCAS transcripts and the HESI score report, i.e. required of all applicants as part of the initial application itself, not a secondary invitation-only step.]

programs.notes: RESIDENCY: No restriction on applying/attending as a non-resident, but tuition differs sharply by residency status ($484.82/SCH resident vs $1,043.57/SCH non-resident). TX residency must be affirmatively established and approved by UH's Residency Determination process (12 consecutive months domicile + intent,  | Q1 IN-PROGRESS PREREQS — answer is the strict reading: UH's FAQ and admission-requirements pages state repeatedly and verbatim 'All prerequisite course work must be completed and official transcripts must be submitted to NursingCAS by the deadline – no exceptions!' and 'No in-progress courses will be accepted.' This is a hard completed-AND-transcripted-by-deadline rule. UH's own checklist recommends transcripts arrive at least 6 weeks before the deadline. An Aug 1 microbiology completion against an Aug 31 deadline is tight but survivable only if the grade posts fast and the transcript is requested/sent/verified within ~3-4 weeks — real risk, not a sure thing; request the transcript the instant the grade posts. Q2 TEXAS CORE / TEXAS GOVERNMENT — a LIVE, credible dealbreaker-level risk, NOT resolved in the applicant's favor. UH requires the full Texas Core Curriculum (42 hours, including Government/Political Science and American History) completed 'no exceptions' before the deadline. UH's own text on out-of-state degree holders describes a discretionary, course-by-course equivalency review, NOT an automatic waiver. Separately, Texas Education Code §51.301/§51.302 is STATE LAW requiring 6 SCH of Government/Political Science 'with special emphasis on that of Texas' (Texas Constitution) and 6 SCH of American History for ANY baccalaureate degree from a Texas public university, regardless of prior degrees — and the THECB block-transfer exemption only applies when the full core was completed at another TEXAS PUBLIC institution, not an out-of-state school like UW-Madison. A Wisconsin government course almost certainly does not cover Texas Constitution content. BOTTOM LINE: the applicant should assume they likely need a Texas Government course (e.g. GOVT 2306, available in accelerated formats at TX community colleges) completed and transcripted before the deadline unless UH's equivalency review says otherwise, and should get that determination from UH admissions/registrar immediately given the compressed timeline. American History risk is lower if UW-Madison coursework already included ~6 SCH of general U.S. history. | URGENT — DEADLINE CONFLICT ON UH'S OWN SITE: the official 'Application Deadlines' page lists Second Degree BSN Spring closing Aug 31, matching the known figure and used here. HOWEVER, the Second-Degree-BSN-specific FAQ page (fetched twice, consistent) repeatedly states the prerequisite/transcript deadline is 'July 15' — i.e., today. Best assessment is the FAQ is stale/cross-contaminated from the RN-BSN FAQ and the dedicated deadlines table is current, but this could NOT be fully resolved from public pages. The applicant should call (832-842-8200) or email (nursing@uh.edu) immediately, and/or check the live NursingCAS UH listing, before assuming Aug 31 is safe. TUITION: precisely confirmed via UH's official Undergraduate Tuition (AY2027) page — $484.82/SCH resident × 60 SCH = $29,089.20 (matches applicant's TX-residency plan) vs $1,043.57/SCH × 60 = $62,614.20 OOS. FEES: no single official consolidated figure found for the 3-term (Spring/Summer/Fall) calendar; estimated ≈$3,500 by combining per-term mandatory-fee figures from UH's Required Fees page — treat as rough. Books separately ~$3,500 (matches applicant's known figure, corroborated by a third-party aggregator, whose ~$35,000 implied all-in total suggests fees could run higher than this estimate). GPA: 3.0 cumulative is a hard eligibility floor; 3.0 science GPA is 'expected'/'encouraged for competitiveness,' softer language, mild ambiguity on whether it's an absolute floor. TEAS: confirmed TEAS VII current (one stale PDF references TEAS VI); no official minimum score, but 80+ per section 'highly encouraged' to be competitive; max two attempts. ONLINE LAB: despite ~10 fetch/search attempts across UH's FAQ, requirements, checklist, and policy pages, found no explicit UH statement on prerequisite lab delivery mode — the only 'face-to-face' language found describes UH's own RN-BSN curriculum, not incoming prerequisites. A nearby Houston program (UTHealth Cizik) explicitly rejects online prerequisite labs, suggesting this may be a regional norm, but that is not a UH-specific confirmation — reported 'unknown,' not 'not_accepted,' and flagged as a genuine open risk given both of the applicant's A&P labs were online. NCLEX: 100% first-time pass rate 2023-24 (5th time achieving 100%), college-wide not accelerated-track-specific. NOT FOUND despite real effort: exact app fee, exact reference count, exact deposit, UH-specific essay prompt/word count, formal prerequisite recency policy (none found stated, mild good news for the applicant's 2001-2005 coursework but not written confirmation). CONFIRMED: interview + background check + drug screen required as a final admission contingency; BLS/CPR must be AHA-issued, non-expired, submitted before the application deadline (earlier than typical); face-to-face delivery 5 days/week at Sugar Land, up to 50 hrs/week; Spring-only, one cohort/year, no waitlist, applications don't carry forward. Public secular institution, no religious requirement.

The applicant has a longstanding Texas mailing ad | CNA HARD BLOCKER: The current official Accelerated Second Degree page lists completion of certified nursing assistant training as an academic admission criterion; only certification at admission consideration is phrased as preferred. This corrects the interrupted draft, which had incorrectly treated CNA itself as optional. DEADLINE MECHANICS: Jul 15 is a COMPLETE-BY deadline, not merely submit-by, with NO published grace/late-file window. TTUHSC's Transcript Evaluation FAQ states applicants who won't finish their 40-SCH threshold until after the deadline cannot apply ('the review process commences shortly after the deadline so the 40 credits must be earned and reported on a transcript prior to application deadline'); the admissions FAQ separately confirms 'all materials must be complete by the deadline.' So all required materials — transcripts showing >=40 of 55 prereq SCH earned, >=3 of 5 sciences fully complete, application form, fee, etc. — must be in hand by end of day today. Applicant has Chem + A&P I + A&P II complete (exactly 3 of 5 sciences, satisfying that rule) and Microbiology in-progress/completing Aug 1 2026 (allowed as one of up to 2 sciences that may be in-progress with proof of enrollment) — she appears to satisfy the science-completion rule, but should independently confirm her total prerequisite SCH count clears the 40-of-55 threshold before submitting today. SPRING 2028 CYCLE: not separately published this far out; the May 1–Jul 15 window is described as a standing annual 'Spring Admission Only' policy, so Spring 2028 should follow the same pattern (~May 1, 2027 – Jul 15, 2027) as a fallback if today's cycle is missed — reconfirm closer to the date. TX CORE CURRICULUM: NOT automatically waived by an out-of-state bachelor's degree at TTUHSC specifically. The 2022-23 catalog states verbatim: 'A second bachelor's degree sought by a student who did not complete the core curriculum at a public Texas institution of higher education must include the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center required core curriculum,' and the prerequisites page adds that gen-ed from a 'private or out-of-state institution may not be equivalents of the required Texas Core Curriculum, and may not excuse a student from not completing the core curriculum.' Since the applicant's bachelor's is from UW-Madison (out-of-state), the common 'already have a bachelor's = automatic exemption' assumption does NOT hold here — TTUHSC requires course-by-course evidence of the 42-hour core (see prereq_extras breakdown). Her UW-Madison coursework will likely satisfy most categories course-by-course, but American History (6h) and Government/Political Science (6h) are the categories most likely to need a TX-specific evaluation; she should request a formal transcript evaluation from applynursing@ttuhsc.edu before relying on this program. TUITION: Official TTUHSC Cost of Attendance figures for the Accelerated BSN (matches scout data exactly): IN-STATE = $8,800 tuition + $8,822 fees = $17,622 total; OUT-OF-STATE = $25,160 tuition + $8,822 fees = $33,982 total. See residency_restriction — given her current WI residency and the 12-month durational rule (domicile needed by ~Jan 26, 2026 for a Spring 2027/Jan 26 2027-census start), she should plan financially for the $33,982 OOS total, not the $17,622 in-state total, despite this database's usual convention of assuming TX in-state rates for TX schools. | ONLINE A&P LAB POLICY (accepted, moderate-not-explicit confidence): no TTUHSC page explicitly separates in-person vs. online LAB components from lecture. Best available evidence is the official Transcript Evaluation FAQ (nursing.ttuhsc.edu/nursing/student-affairs/transcript_evaluation.php): Q: 'Can I take the courses online?' A: 'Yes, as long as the courses are taken from a regionally accredited institution, the scores will be accepted. Please contact your school's registrar to determine if they are regionally accredited.' This is an unqualified yes with no lab carve-out anywhere on the site, and TTUHSC does not itself teach these prerequisites (completed beforehand at any accredited institution), so there is no in-house lab-attendance requirement to enforce. Applicant's Chem lab was in-person (moot) and A&P I/II labs were online — should not be a blocker under this policy, but because the source doesn't explicitly say the word 'lab,' recommend she get written confirmation from applynursing@ttuhsc.edu given the stakes. NCLEX: officially reported 2024 first-time NCLEX-RN pass rate = 94.66% (550/581) per Texas BON's April 2025 Board Meeting report (agenda item 3.2.12), listed as 'Texas Tech HSC SON' / Lubbock (US27503600). This is PROGRAM-WIDE across all TTUHSC School of Nursing tracks/sites (Traditional, ABSN incl. San Antonio, Veteran-to-BSN, RN-to-BSN combined) — Texas BON does not report per-site, so no San-Antonio-specific figure exists. TTUHSC's own promotional blog (dailydose.ttuhsc.edu) separately touts 100% pass rates for specific single recent cohorts at individual sites (Dallas ABSN, Amarillo, Mansfield) — these are cherry-picked, not the audited program-wide figure, so I used the official BON number. GPA: 2.5 minimum on BOTH cumulative GPA AND science-prerequisite GPA independently (Chem/A&P I/A&P II/Micro/Patho), 3.0+ preferred for both, maintained at both application and program start. ESSAY/INTERVIEW/REFERENCES: interview (face-to-face, Zoom, or video-recorded, professional attire) is required only for applicants advanced past initial holistic screening; essay required only for interview invitees, not at initial application. No page for this specific track lists letters of recommendation as required (Traditional BSN explicitly says LORs NOT required; only graduate MSN/DNP explicitly requires 3) — could not find an explicit statement either way for Second-Degree/ABSN, so references_count is null rather than guessed; likely not required but verify directly. EXAM: no TEAS/HESI/GRE requirement found anywhere for this track; Traditional BSN explicitly dropped TEAS starting Summer 2020, and the 2022-23 catalog's admission-requirements section has no exam-score line item for Second-Degree either. APPLICATION FEE & DEPOSIT: no dollar figures published anywhere despite extensive searching of ttuhsc.edu, applynursing.ttuhsc.edu, the catalog, and FAQ — only that 'all application fees and placement fees/enrollment deposits are non-refundable,' with deposit instructions 'included in the enrollment offer letter' (disclosed only post-admission). Do not confuse with the unrelated $75 ApplyTexas fee, which is for a separate process (transient/visiting-student enrollment in a standalone TTU-Lubbock prerequisite course like Pathophysiology), not the nursing-program application itself (which runs through applynursing.ttuhsc.edu, confirming app_system=direct, not NursingCAS). IN-PROGRESS RULE (precise mechanics): of 55 total prerequisite SCH, >=40 must be fully earned/on an official transcript by the Jul 15 deadline; up to 15 may show 'proof of enrollment' only. Independently, of the 5 named science courses (Pathophysiology, Microbiology, A&P I, A&P II, Chemistry), >=3 must be fully complete by the deadline; up to 2 may be in-progress with proof of enrollment. ALL prerequisites must be complete with a C-or-better before the first day of class (Jan 11, 2027). CNA (2026-07-15 AUDIT CORRECTION): Completion of CNA training is a listed admission criterion. Certification at admission consideration is preferred, but the training itself is not described as optional. Because the applicant cannot complete CNA training before January 2027, this program is a hard blocker absent a written school exception. TUITION SOURCE RECONCILIATION: TTUHSC's fiscal per-SCH schedule (Statutory $50/SCH resident or $478/SCH nonresident + Designated Tuition $188.29/SCH FY27) would imply resident tuition-only near $14,536 for 61 SCH, higher than the COA page's $8,800 — I deferred to the COA page's official pre-built total (which matches scout data exactly, $8,800 tuition/$8,822 fees resident and $25,160 tuition/$8,822 fees nonresident, i.e. $33,982 OOS total) since it is TTUHSC's own purpose-built aggregate for financial aid/cost estimation and the per-SCH fiscal collateral page covers multiple TTUHSC schools where the extraction may have blended rows from other programs (e.g., graduate nursing's higher designated tuition). Start date Jan 11, 2027 confirmed directly from the official TTUHSC School of Nursing 2026-2027 Academic Calendar PDF (revised 01.12.2026), row 'SPRING 2027 Traditional, ABSN, Graduate Level, RN-BSN', Add/Drop period '01/11 - 01/26', Official Census I Date 1/26/2027 — matches scout data exactly. TTUHSC is a Texas public state institution (Texas Tech University System) — not religious. San Antonio is one of several TTUHSC instructional sites (Abilene, Amarillo, Austin, Dallas, Lubbock, Odessa, San Antonio); didactic coursework is delivered online system-wide with local clinical placements plus an assigned 'clinical coach,' consistent with scout notes. Curriculum confirmed via 2022-23 catalog: 3 semesters (20/21/20 SCH = 61 total), all NURS-prefix courses. F1/F2 international students are NOT eligible for this program since it's fully online — not relevant to this applicant but worth flagging generally.

programs.notes:
RESIDENCY: No Arizona-residency admission restriction found. Nonresidents are eligible and are billed the published nonresident rate; clinical travel may occur statewide. | (1) Application window CONFIRMED: Oct 7-Nov 18, 2026 for the Spring/Jan 2027 cohort, verified identically across 3 independent fetches (nau.edu/nursing/how-to-apply page, fetched twice with full raw-text dumps, plus the live application portal programapplication.nau.edu). HESI A2 sub-deadline CONFIRMED as Oct 11-Nov 22, 2026 (same 3 sources). Both exactly match scout data. (2) Online A&P lab policy: COULD NOT DETERMINE. After ~15 targeted searches/fetches of NAU's nursing prerequisite pages, transfer-credit policy, academic catalog, and FAQ, no explicit public statement exists on whether online-lab A&P I/II (BIO 201L/202L) transfer credit is accepted. NAU's published transfer policy addresses only grade/accreditation ('C or better from an accredited institution'), not delivery mode. This is very likely handled case-by-case by an academic advisor during transcript evaluation (NAU's own applied process explicitly inserts an advisor consultation step before nursing application). Applicant MUST contact nursing@nau.edu / accelerated.nursing@nau.edu (928-523-2671) directly and get this in writing before relying on it. (3) OOS tuition: CONFIRMED $30,000/yr base + $2,757/yr fees ($1,625 mandatory + $1,132 college) = $32,757/yr, from NAU's official 2026-27 nonresident tuition page — exact match to scout figures. BUT this 12-month program (Jan 2027-~Jan 2028) spans NAU's 2026-27 AND 2027-28 tuition-rate years, and 2027-28 rates are not yet published (as of this research), so full-program cost is likely somewhat higher than $32,757; treat that figure as a floor, not a final total. A secondary source also claims an additional $2,400 ABSN-specific program fee that I could not confirm or deny via a primary NAU source. See notes for full math and a $2,400 program-fee caveat. | CAMPUS: The current nursing application/deadline page assigns all Accelerated BSN cycles, including Spring 2027, to North Valley, so this row is correctly modeled there. A current NAU catalog/program page is internally inconsistent: it retains older Flagstaff-only language while also listing both Flagstaff and North Valley and later describing North Valley availability. For the January 2027 application use North Valley, but confirm the cohort location in writing before enrolling. No Tucson ABSN is published. START DATE: Jan 11, 2027 confirmed as NAU's Spring 2027 first day of classes per NAU Registrar academic-calendar pages (in.nau.edu/registrar/important-dates/, spring-2027-enrollment-calendar/).

ONLINE A&P LAB POLICY = UNKNOWN (the flagged critical issue): No official NAU page states whether online-lab A&P transfer credit is accepted or rejected. Recommend applicant email nursing@nau.edu / accelerated.nursing@nau.edu now (928-523-2671), explicitly ask about BIO 201L/202L online-lab transfer equivalency, and get a written answer before the Oct 7 window opens. Do not assume acceptance.

TUITION MATH: NAU's official 2026-27 nonresident undergraduate flat annual rate (nau.edu/fees/upcoming-tuition/) = $30,000 tuition + $1,625 mandatory fees + $1,132 college fees = $32,757 total -- exact match to scout data's '$30,000/yr + $2,757 fees'. However the 12-month program spans TWO NAU tuition-rate years (2026-27 for Spring+Summer 2027; 2027-28, not yet published, for Fall 2027 onward), and it's unclear whether the flat annual rate (typically assumes Fall+Spring, 2 semesters) already covers the Summer term the ABSN also runs or whether summer bills separately -- NAU doesn't break this out by term for nursing. A secondary ABSN-directory site (absnprograms.org) additionally claims a $2,400 ABSN-specific 'program fee' ($800/semester x 3 semesters); I could NOT confirm or deny this via a primary NAU source (the CHHS program-fee PDF fetched as corrupted binary; nau.edu/nursing/nursing-program-fees/ had no dollar figures). tuition_total/fees_total above reflect ONLY the confirmed one-year 2026-27 published rate -- treat as a FLOOR. Realistic all-in cost is likely $33,000-$37,000+ once the second tuition year and any program fee are factored in. Get an official cost estimate from NAU Student Accounts (928-523-3122) once admitted.

GPA: Two figures exist -- a university-wide 2.0 minimum 'cumulative GPA on all work attempted at NAU' (baseline good-standing rule, not nursing-specific) vs. a nursing-specific 'minimum 3.0 in prerequisite courses' for ABSN admission ('most successful applicants have a GPA well above 3.0'). Reported gpa_min=3.0 as the operative admission bar.

ESSAYS/REFERENCES/INTERVIEW/DEPOSIT/APP FEE: None of these were explicitly mentioned anywhere in official NAU sources despite dedicated searches (personal statement, letters of recommendation, interview, deposit, application fee) and fetching the application portal itself. What IS explicitly stated: admission is numbers-driven -- 'HESI A2 exam results will be used as part of the process of screening and ranking applicants' alongside prerequisite GPA, cycle described as 'first-come, first-served' within qualified applicants. No essay/reference/interview requirement surfaced anywhere, consistent with a metrics-only screen unlike many holistic-review ABSN programs. essays=[], references_count=null, interview='none' are best-evidence INFERENCES from absence of any mention, not explicit confirmations -- verify directly with nursing@nau.edu before assuming no essay is needed. Application fee amount was not locatable anywhere.

HESI A2 MINIMUM SCORE: Not found on any NAU-specific page. Comparable AZ programs (e.g. University of Arizona College of Nursing) use 75% combined-average across Math/Reading/Vocabulary/Biology, but this is NOT confirmed as NAU's own threshold -- do not assume it applies here.

IN-PROGRESS PREREQ POLICY: NAU explicitly allows '5 or fewer in-progress prerequisite courses at the time of application,' but ALL prerequisites must be completed with a C or better by the FIRST DAY of the program. For this applicant, microbiology (only outstanding prereq) completes Aug 1, 2026, more than 2 months before the Oct 7 application window opens -- so 0 courses will be in-progress at application time, well clear of the 5-course allowance. Non-issue for this applicant.

PREREQUISITES: The ACCELERATED-specific list (confirmed via 2 independent fetches of the official catalog, plan=NURABSNXPB) totals exactly 27 units: BIO 201/201L + BIO 202/202L (A&P I/II, 12 units) + BIO 205/205L (Microbiology, 3 units) + BIO 320 (Pathophysiology, 3 units) = 15-unit 'Biology Sequence'; PSY 101 (Intro Psych) + PSY 240 (Developmental Psychology, confirmed via catalog course title -- this is the 'lifespan' tag) = 6 units; NTS 135 (Nutrition) = 3 units; STA 270 or PSY 230 (Statistics) = 3 units. Standalone Chemistry is NOT part of the Accelerated-specific 27-unit list (a 'BIO 181 or CHM 130+130L' gateway-science requirement exists only in NAU's separate Traditional/general BSN 30-32-unit prereq list, a different pathway) -- so applicant's completed General Chemistry isn't formally required for THIS program, though it doesn't hurt. No sociology, ethics, or standalone general-biology course required.

PREREQ RECENCY: No explicit recency/expiration policy found publicly. Not a practical concern here regardless -- applicant's relevant science prerequisites (Chem, A&P I/II, Micro, Stats, Nutrition, Developmental Psych) were all completed in 2026.

NCLEX PASS RATE: NAU's own official page commits only to 'consistently over 90%' (qualitative, no specific year, not split by ABSN vs Traditional/Compressed). A secondary aggregator (nurse.org NCLEX scorecard) cites '94.5% (2025)' for NAU, but I could NOT independently verify this against the primary source -- the Arizona State Board of Nursing's own PDF pass-rate reports (azbn.gov) returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt (automated access blocked). Treat 94.5%/2025 as secondary-sourced/unverified; '>90% consistently' is the only NAU-primary-confirmed figure.

CERTIFICATIONS/BACKGROUND CHECK/IMMUNIZATIONS: NAU's College of Nursing states health-and-safety requirements for clinical participation include background checks, drug/nicotine testing, and immunizations (2x MMR required; Hep A/B, Varicella, annual flu strongly recommended). A now-removed post-admission checklist reportedly listed CPR/BLS and fingerprint clearance, but that claim could not be re-fetched from a current primary page. The structured certifications array is therefore left empty rather than guessed; confirm BLS/CPR timing directly after admission. RELIGIOUS: NAU is a public Arizona Board of Regents university -- no religious affiliation, mission, or coursework anywhere in the program.

programs.notes: RESIDENCY: No state-residency requirement to apply/enroll, but applicants must live within commuting distance of Lynnwood, WA (16 miles north of Seattle) to attend mandatory weekly in-person skills/simulation labs and complete local clinical rotations. | RELIGION REQUIREMENT (critical secondary question): CONFIRMED REQUIRED, and this is the most important finding for PLU. The ABSN-specific requirements page (absn.plu.edu/admissions/absn-requirements/, fetched directly) states verbatim: 'You must take four credits in the Academic Study of Religion category to graduate, and these credits must be completed at PLU' -- must be taken AT PLU, cannot be transferred in. I initially found this sits outside the 68-credit/16-month nursing curriculum itself (the semester-by-semester ABSN curriculum is 100% NURS-prefixed courses with no religion course listed), which could read as 'not really required for ABSN.' But a second search confirmed PLU's institutional policy for students entering with an existing bachelor's degree: they're granted senior standing and have ALL general-education requirements waived EXCEPT four hours of Academic Study of Religion, four hours of Global Engagement, and the Culminating Experience -- religion is explicitly NOT waived even for second-degree/already-have-a-bachelor's students. So this is a real, additional, non-negotiable requirement for an ABSN student to actually receive the PLU BSN degree -- applicant should ask their admissions rep exactly when/how this 4-credit course is scheduled relative to the 4 nursing semesters, since it's not on the official curriculum plan. Lutheran tradition (ELCA) confirmed via PLU's own about/history pages and cross-referenced against ELCA's own regional-institution listings. ONLINE LAB POLICY (critical question): Best available evidence says ACCEPTED, but it's an inference, not a page-literal ABSN confirmation. PLU's Entry-Level MSN (ELMSN) prerequisites page -- same School of Nursing, same course list style (A&P I/II 'with lab within last six years', Microbiology 'with lab within last six years'), literally states: 'Courses which require a lab may be completed either on-site or online.' I could not find this exact sentence anywhere on the ABSN-specific prerequisites page (absn.plu.edu/admissions/absn-prerequisites/), which lists the identical courses (BIOL 205/206, BIOL 201, CHEM 105) with the identical 6-year recency window but is silent on delivery format. Given it's the same nursing school, same course numbers, same recency rule, I'm reasonably confident this extends to ABSN, but recommend applicant get explicit written confirmation from an ABSN admissions rep before relying on it, since a wrong guess here would be a costly hard-blocker mistake. IMPORTANT CAUTION: a WebSearch summarizer (not a direct page fetch) at one point fabricated the phrase 'on-site lab' as if it were literal ABSN page text describing course titles -- I verified this was NOT actually on the page via a verbatim re-fetch, so I've discounted that fabricated claim entirely and relied only on the MSN-page quote above, which I directly verified. | TUITION/FEES: tuition_total $69,700 is precise and confirmed (68 credits x $1,025/credit, official absn.plu.edu/admissions/tuition/ page). fees_total is the literal 'Total ABSN program fees (approximate): $5,750' figure from that same official page -- but that page ALSO separately states 'Total estimated cost (tuition + fees): $77,205', which is $1,755 MORE than 69,700+5,750=75,450. The gap likely comes from additional per-semester course/lab fees mentioned on the page but not itemized into the summary 'approximate' figure (page lists matriculation fee, technology fee, wellness/telehealth fee, Kaplan fee, CB Bridges background-check/drug-screen fee, CPNW consortium fee, and 'course fees charged per semester' without dollar amounts for most). Use $77,205 as the safer all-in planning number; treat $5,750 as a floor, not a ceiling, on fees. APPLICATION SYSTEM: Confirmed direct (not NursingCAS) -- PLU does not appear in NursingCAS's official Explore Schools directory, and PLU uses its own Banner-based application login (bss.plu.edu). However, ESSAYS and the $73 APP FEE are sourced from PLU's GENERAL nursing application page (www.plu.edu/nursing/application/), which explicitly describes itself as covering the Traditional BSN program and only mentions ABSN Lynnwood as a pointer to a separate site/system -- I could NOT confirm these apply to the ABSN-Lynnwood-specific application flow (which appears to run through a lead-gen 'talk to an admissions rep' intake at absn.plu.edu that never mentions essays, an app fee, or an interview across half a dozen dedicated admissions pages I read in full). Treat essay/app-fee/interview values as low-confidence carryovers from a possibly-different track, not confirmed ABSN facts. INTERVIEW: Reported 'none' by inference -- PLU describes its ABSN admission process in step-by-step detail on multiple pages ('contact rep → plan for prerequisites → fulfill requirements → submit application' / 'talk with rep → make a plan → submit application') and never once mentions an interview step, in contrast to Mount Sinai where an interview is consistently and specifically described. This is an absence-based inference, not an explicit 'no interview' statement -- flag as medium confidence. CERTIFICATIONS/REFERENCES: Could not confirm a specific BLS/CPR requirement or reference-letter count for ABSN despite extensive searching (virtually all pre-licensure nursing programs require BLS before clinicals, so this is very likely required in practice, but I won't assert it as confirmed since I couldn't source it). GPA/PREREQS: 3.0 cumulative GPA minimum + B- minimum in each of 7 prerequisite courses (Microbiology, A&P I, A&P II, Chemistry of Life, Development Across the Lifespan, Introductory Statistics, Nutrition in Healthcare) -- all 7 map cleanly onto the standard taxonomy (no extras beyond it; no separate general psych, sociology, or ethics requirement, unlike Mount Sinai). 6-year recency window applies per the official prerequisites page footnote (attached to the full course list). IN-PROGRESS POLICY: Found stated for prerequisites broadly ('you can start the application process if you have not completed all prerequisites... upload an unofficial transcript showing the in-progress course(s)... all prerequisites must be finished before the program officially begins') -- this matches applicant's Aug 1, 2026 microbiology completion against a Feb 2027 start, well in advance. RESIDENCY: Confirmed to be a practical commuting-distance requirement (weekly in-person labs in Lynnwood + local clinicals), not a legal state-residency requirement -- Wisconsin residency is not disqualifying. NCLEX: Official WA State Board of Nursing (WABON) February 2026 school report PDF shows TWO Pacific Lutheran rows: 'Pacific Lutheran University - BSN' (2025: 191/222 = 86.04%) and 'Pacific Lutheran University - GE' (2025: 17/20 = 85.00%). I interpreted 'GE' as 'Generic' entry (i.e., prelicensure second-degree/accelerated entry -- matching ABSN's much smaller per-cohort size) and reported that row, since the 'BSN' row's much larger n is more consistent with PLU's traditional 4-year Tacoma-campus program (possibly combined with ABSN) -- but WABON's report does not define 'GE' on the page itself, so this is an interpretation, not a certainty; the 86.04% 'BSN' figure is the alternative if 'GE' means something else. START DATE: No January cohort exists at PLU -- cohorts start Feb/Jun/Sep only, so Feb 1, 2027 is the closest available start to the applicant's January 2027 target (about one month later).

programs.notes: SPECIFIC COHORT DATE: Not found published anywhere. GCU confirms 3 annual ABSN start months (Jan/May/Sept) at every site incl. Sandy, UT, but exact days are counselor/form-gated, not published. GCU's general academic calendar shows Spring semesters starting the first Monday of January (Jan 5, 2026; Jan 4, 2027 confirmed on gcu.edu/academics/calendar), so 2027-01-04 is my best estimate for the Jan 2027 ABSN cohort, but this is inferred, not ABSN-specific-confirmed. RECOMMENDATION: contact a GCU ABSN counselor directly for the exact Jan 2027 date. ONLINE LAB POLICY: Genuinely unpublished. GCU's prerequisites page requires A&P/Chem/Micro labs as credit-bearing line items but never states a delivery-format (online vs in-person) rule for prerequisites completed at OTHER institutions before applying. Given GCU's own transfer-credit process is individualized (counselor-driven credit evaluation of official transcripts), the applicant's online A&P I/II labs will likely be evaluated case-by-case rather than blanket-rejected, but this cannot be confirmed from public sources. CHRISTIAN WORLDVIEW / RELIGIOUS COURSEWORK: Likely still required despite the second-degree/bachelor's-holder pathway. CWV-101 or CWV-301 (Christian Worldview, 4 credits) is explicitly described as 'foundational to GCU's identity' and non-transferable — the one gen-ed course NOT waived even for students whose other gen-ed is fully satisfied by transfer credit. A companion course, University Foundations (UNV-103/303, 4 credits), appears similarly non-waivable but is a secular 'college success skills' course, not religious. | TUITION MATH: $850/credit x 63 accelerated-portion credits = $53,550, confirmed directly on GCU's official ABSN tuition page; no separate Utah/Sandy pricing found — GCU appears to charge one flat national rate across all ABSN sites. Additional unquantified fees exist (health insurance, clinical-placement software, books/materials, graduation fee); budget extra beyond $53,550. GPA: two thresholds — 3.0 cumulative for overall admission AND 3.25 cumulative specifically across the 9 prerequisite courses/labs. PREREQUISITES: GCU's official list (fetched 3x, consistent) is narrower than most competing ABSN programs — only Human A&P II (BIO-202, not A&P I by name), Microbiology, Chemistry (Gen/Organic/Biochem combined), Applied Nutrition, Applied Pathophysiology, and Lifespan Development (PSY-357), totaling 9 course/lab line items = 28 credits. Notably absent as standalone requirements: Statistics, Sociology, general Biology, Ethics. Oddly, A&P I is never named on GCU's own page even though A&P II presupposes it — flagging for awareness, not treating as resolved. Recency: 'C or higher within 7 years' applies uniformly to ALL 9 prerequisites — moot for this applicant since everything is 2026-dated. IMPORTANT CAUTION: multiple AI-generated search summaries conflated 'Grand Canyon University' (this program, gcu.edu, Phoenix AZ) with 'Georgian Court University' (also self-styled 'GCU,' Lakewood NJ, georgian.edu) — a Statistics-prerequisite claim and a 'May 8, 2026 application deadline' both traced back to Georgian Court and were EXCLUDED as not applicable to Grand Canyon. NCLEX/ACCREDITATION: Sandy, UT NCLEX first-time pass rates were strong (100% in 2025 on n=17 full-year per secondary aggregation, 95% in 2024 on n=19) but could not be independently verified via Utah's own DOPL PDF (fetch tool couldn't parse its table format) — secondary-sourced, not primary-verified. CCNE accreditation applies at the BSN-program level; no pending-status caveat was found for the Utah/Sandy site (opened 2022, multiple years of reported NCLEX outcomes), suggesting established rather than pending accreditation — inferred from absence of a caveat. APPLICATION PROCESS: GCU uses its own direct application (apply.gcu.edu), not NursingCAS; process is counselor-driven (transcript review -> complete prerequisites -> informal phone pre-admission interview -> submit application -> HESI A2). No application fee and no essay/reference-letter requirement found anywhere despite repeated targeted searches. HESI A2 minimums: >=80% Math/Reading/Grammar/Vocabulary; >=75% A&P section. Deposit: none found in any official GCU tuition/admissions material, reported as null rather than guessed. Residency: GCU is private with one flat per-credit rate; no in-state/OOS distinction and no residency requirement — Wisconsin residency is a non-issue here.
